rulings.question: Where does a Flow spell countered by Abandon go?
rulings.answer: If no other replacement effects apply, it is banished rather than returned to its owner's hand. Abandon's "Counter a spell" instruction targets a finalized spell on the chain. 355.10 355.9.a.2 Countering would clear that spell from the chain and put it in the trash. 426.1.a 426.1.a.1 Abandon's later instruction replaces putting it in the trash with returning it to its owner's hand. 158.2 369.1 Because Abandon's counter, rather than the spell's own execution, makes it leave the chain, the delayed replacement effect created by [Flow] also applies and would banish it instead. 829.1.b.1 Both replacement effects apply to the same departure event, so the spell's controller chooses their order. 372 The result is the same in either order. If [Flow] applies first, the spell is banished instead of going to the trash, so Abandon no longer has a qualifying event to replace. 370.1 If Abandon applies first, it replaces the original event with the spell leaving the chain for its owner's hand. 370.1.b That replacement event still makes the spell leave the chain, so [Flow] applies and banishes it instead. 370.2 An additional replacement effect joins this ordering and can change the final destination. 370.2 372

rulings.question: Does Abandoned Hall's ability trigger if the spell is countered?
rulings.answer: No. Abandoned Hall's "when a player plays a spell" condition is fulfilled only when that spell finishes resolving. 420.4.a A countered spell does not resolve and is not considered played for triggered abilities, so Abandoned Hall's ability is not put on the chain. 420.4.a.1

rulings.question: Can a unit moved into or away from Abandoned Hall by a spell be targeted?
rulings.answer: After the spell resolves, Abandoned Hall can choose only a unit at Abandoned Hall controlled by the player who played that spell. 190.6.c 355.9.b 355.10 Moved into Abandoned Hall: The unit can be chosen if the spell's player controls the unit when Abandoned Hall's triggered ability finalizes. Moved away from Abandoned Hall: The unit cannot be chosen, even if the spell's player controls the unit, because the unit is no longer at Abandoned Hall. Abandoned Hall's trigger condition is not fulfilled until the spell has finished resolving. 420.4.a The resulting ability is then added as a pending item. 383.3 402.1 Abandoned Hall's triggered ability chooses its target when the ability finalizes. 403.2

rulings.question: Can Abandoned Hall's triggered ability choose a unit that a spell plays there?
rulings.answer: Yes, if the player who played the spell controls that unit when the ability finalizes. The spell starts playing the unit during its own resolution, so the unit waits on the chain as a pending item. 354.2 354.3 When the spell finishes resolving, Abandoned Hall's triggered ability is added as a newer pending item. 420.4.a 383.3 402.1 The unit finalizes before that newer ability because pending items finalize in append order. 337.1.b It immediately resolves and enters Abandoned Hall. 337.2 359.2.c When the triggered ability later finalizes, it can select the unit played by the spell as its target. 190.6.c 355.9.b 355.10 403.2

rulings.question: When is my "next Ending Phase" for Akali, Brash?
rulings.answer: Your "next Ending Phase" is whichever of your Ending Phases begins first after Akali's second-move triggered ability resolves. The ability creates the play permission when it executes. 407.5 That permission remains active only for the time stated by the effect. 391.4 392 Earlier in your turn: If the ability resolves before that turn's Ending Phase begins, that same Ending Phase is next. 316.9.b The permission ends when the game enters that phase. During your Ending Phase or another player's turn: If the ability resolves during your Ending Phase, that phase has already begun. If it resolves during another player's turn, that turn's Ending Phase isn't yours. In either case, your next Ending Phase begins on your following turn. 115.1.c 317.3 The permission ends when that phase begins.

rulings.question: Can an opponent's Deathknell target Akali, Silent after combat damage?
rulings.answer: Yes, Akali can be targeted by enemy [Deathknell] abilities until combat ends, as long as she remains at the battlefield with a combat designation. Combat has three steps: Combat Showdown Step. 466 Combat Damage Step. 467 Resolution Step. 468 The combat cleanup kills lethally damaged units. 468.1 323.4 A [Deathknell] trigger is added to the chain before its unit moves to the trash. 808.1.d.2 Any targets are chosen when those abilities finalize. 403.2 Those abilities fully resolve before combat proceeds to determining the result. 468.2 Combat ends only at the final part of this step. 468.7 Only then is Akali's combat designation removed, so she stops being in combat and her restriction against enemy spells and abilities applies again. 468.7.a 740.2.c This is why Ruined Rex 's [Deathknell] can choose her after Rex dies to combat damage.

rulings.question: If my Dazzling Aurora plays Akshan, Mischievous at the end of my turn, will the Dazzling Aurora I take from my opponent trigger that turn?
rulings.answer: No. You gain control of the enemy Dazzling Aurora after its end-of-turn trigger condition has already been checked. "At the end of your turn" refers to the Ending Step's end-of-turn point. 317.1.a 383.1 At that point, the enemy Dazzling Aurora is still controlled by your opponent, so its controller-relative "your turn" condition is not fulfilled. 191.5.a 383.2.c Your Dazzling Aurora's end-of-turn ability plays Akshan after that point in the turn has been reached. After Akshan enters the board, his play effect is added to the chain as a pending item. 383.4.a 383.4.a.2 You gain control of the enemy Dazzling Aurora only when that ability later resolves. 407.5 If you take control of an enemy Dazzling Aurora before the Ending Step and still control it at the end-of-turn point, it triggers normally.

rulings.question: If my opponent and I each use Akshan, Mischievous to take the same gear, who controls it when either Akshan dies?
rulings.answer: After both play effects have resolved, if either Akshan dies, the gear is controlled by the player whose control effect remains. While both effects remain, the player whose effect was generated most recently controls the gear. Each resolved play effect creates a delayed passive ability, a control effect that remains active until that Akshan leaves the board. 391.4 392 While both effects remain, they change the gear's controller in the same trait-altering layer. 479.2.a Neither effect changes the other's existence, scope, or result, so no dependency is established. 480.1.a 480.1.b 480.1.c Timestamp order therefore applies. 482 Each effect's timestamp is established when it begins applying, and the newer effect applies last and determines who controls the gear. 482.1 482.3 When an Akshan dies, it moves from the board to the trash, ending that Akshan's control effect and leaving the other effect to determine control. 429.2

rulings.question: How are targets chosen when playing Alpha Strike?
rulings.answer: Alpha Strike's controller chooses its targets while finalizing the spell, in the following order. 355.5 355.14.b Every chosen unit is a target and must be a legal choice. 355.8 355.9.b 355.10 355.14.a Choose one friendly unit. Check that unit's current might after applying all might-changing effects (its effective might). 143.2.a 143.2.a.1 Then choose any legal number of enemy units at battlefields, up to that amount; Alpha Strike does not require every enemy unit across every battlefield to be chosen. 355.14.c Pay the mandatory additional cost for each chosen enemy unit with [Deflect]. 740.1.b 809.1.c 356.2.a.2 Once Alpha Strike finishes finalizing, its target choices cannot change unless a spell or ability instructs a player to make new choices. 355.15

rulings.question: When and how is Alpha Strike's damage distributed?
rulings.answer: Alpha Strike's controller chooses how to distribute its damage during resolution, not while choosing targets. 355.14.e As Alpha Strike begins resolving, determine which chosen units remain legal targets. 359.3.e.2 If the friendly target is illegal, Alpha Strike deals no damage because that target provides no usable might. 359.3.f.2.a If no enemy target remains legal, Alpha Strike deals no damage because its damage instruction does not execute. 359.3.e.7 Use the friendly target's current might after applying all might-changing effects (its effective might) as the amount of damage to distribute. 143.2.a 143.2.a.1 Because Alpha Strike does not specify a different time, check that might when the damage instruction executes. 359.3.f.1 359.3.f.2 If there are more remaining enemy targets than damage, choose exactly enough of those units to cease being targets so the number of targets does not exceed the available damage. 355.14.h 355.14.h.1 Distribute all available damage among the remaining enemy targets, assigning at least 1 damage to each. 355.14.f 355.14.g If only one enemy target remains, assign all available damage to it.

rulings.question: What happens if Alpha Strike's friendly target has its might reduced?
rulings.answer: If the friendly target remains legal but has lower might when Alpha Strike's damage instruction executes, Alpha Strike uses that reduced might as the amount of damage to split. 359.3.f.1 359.3.f.2 If there is not enough damage to assign at least 1 to every enemy target, Alpha Strike's controller must remove exactly enough enemy units from Alpha Strike's targets and cannot remove extras to concentrate the damage. 355.14.f 355.14.g 355.14.h 355.14.h.1 Example You chose a friendly Pakaa Cub with 3 , then chose 3 enemy units. Before Alpha Strike resolves, an opponent plays Stupefy targeting Pakaa Cub, reducing it to 2 . You must choose exactly 1 enemy unit to cease being a target. You cannot drop a second target to deal both points of damage to one unit. A negative might value counts as 0 when Alpha Strike references it. 143.2.c If Alpha Strike has 0 damage to split, every enemy target ceases being a target because each remaining target would have to receive at least 1 damage. 355.14.f 355.14.g 355.14.h

rulings.question: What if the chosen friendly unit leaves the board or becomes illegal before Alpha Strike resolves?
rulings.answer: Alpha Strike deals no damage if the chosen friendly unit is an illegal target when the spell resolves. An illegal friendly target provides no might that Alpha Strike can use for its damage instruction. 359.3.f.1 359.3.f.2.a Alpha Strike does not require the chosen friendly unit to be at a particular location, so moving between board locations does not by itself make it illegal. 359.3.e.2 If it stays on the board but temporarily stops being a unit or stops being friendly, it is legal again if it meets every targeting requirement at resolution. 359.3.e.3 If the target changes to or from a non-board zone, it remains illegal even if it returns before resolution because it is a new object. 359.3.e.4

rulings.question: What if a chosen enemy unit leaves a battlefield or becomes illegal before Alpha Strike resolves?
rulings.answer: An enemy unit takes no damage if it remains an illegal target when Alpha Strike resolves. 359.3.e.2 359.3.e.5 If the unit stays on the board but moves to base, stops being an enemy, or otherwise stops meeting Alpha Strike's description, it is legal again if it meets every requirement before resolution. 359.3.e.2 359.3.e.3 If it changes to or from a non-board zone, it remains illegal even if it returns. 359.3.e.4 If every chosen enemy unit is illegal, Alpha Strike deals no damage because its damage instruction does not execute. 359.3.e.7 If one or more enemy targets remain legal, Alpha Strike distributes damage among them only if the friendly target is also legal 359.3.f.2.a and positive damage remains after any required target removal. 359.3.e.8 355.14.f 355.14.g 355.14.h

rulings.question: How does Aphelios, Exalted interact with Svellsongur and Shady Spectacles?
rulings.answer: Aphelios triggers once when either Svellsongur or Shady Spectacles is attached to him, but another unit that becomes a copy of Aphelios through Shady Spectacles does not trigger. Earlier Svellsongur ruling The January 2026 Spiritforged FAQ ruled that Svellsongur copied Aphelios's ability in time for both instances to trigger. The August 2026 Vendetta FAQ expressly reverses that ruling because the attachment happens before the copy action. Each "As this is attached" ability replaces the attachment event with that same event plus a separate copy action. 369.1 370.1.b.1 Game actions are processed one at a time, so Aphelios's trigger condition is checked after the attachment event and his ability is added to the chain before the copy action continues. 303.1 383.2.c 402.1 402.2 With Svellsongur, that pending trigger is created before Svellsongur copies Aphelios's effect text. The newly copied text does not look back and trigger from the attachment that already occurred, so there is no second trigger. With Shady Spectacles attached to Aphelios, his trigger is similarly created before he becomes a copy of the chosen unit. If Shady Spectacles is instead attached to another unit and that unit becomes a copy of Aphelios, the unit did not have Aphelios's ability when the attachment event occurred, so it does not trigger at all.

rulings.question: Does Applied Researchers reduce Repeat, Flow, and Deflect costs?
rulings.answer: Yes, provided Applied Researchers is [Empowered] and the cost belongs to a spell. Its [Empowered] ability grants this discount only while it has the [Empowered] status. 828.1.b.1 [Repeat] is an optional additional cost. 820.1 [Deflect] imposes a mandatory additional cost on a spell or ability that targets the permanent with [Deflect]. 809.1.d Discounts can reduce both kinds of additional costs, including to zero. 356.4.f A [Flow] cost is an alternate cost that replaces a spell's base cost during finalization. 829.1.c.1 Applied Researchers' discount is applied afterward when determining the spell's total cost. 356.1 356.4 Because Applied Researchers' discount applies only to spells, it cannot reduce a [Repeat] or [Deflect] cost paid while playing an ability. 820.1.a 809.1.d

rulings.question: Can Applied Researchers reduce Shock Blast's cost to zero?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Applied Researchers is [Empowered], you can play Shock Blast for . Applied Researchers itself satisfies Shock Blast's requirement that you control something that is [Empowered], so both cards' discounts apply. Both abilities discount Shock Blast's total cost during the Determine Total Cost step of playing it. 356.4 Discounts that apply to the total cost may be applied in any order. 356.4.d 356.4.d.1 A minimum imposed by one discount applies only to that discount. 356.4.e Cost Sequence Base cost: Shock Blast starts at . Applied Researchers reduction: Reduce that cost by , leaving . Applied Researchers minimum: The reduced cost remains above its minimum of . Shock Blast reduction: Reduce the remaining energy cost by , leaving . Applying the discounts in the opposite order would leave the spell costing , but you may choose the order that results in the lower cost.

rulings.question: Can I use Arcane Shift to banish the only unit I own and control at a battlefield I control, then play it there again?
rulings.answer: Yes, as long as the unit is not a token and you control that battlefield. For a non-token unit, by the time battlefield control is checked, the unit's owner has started playing it, leaving the unit pending on the chain while Arcane Shift finishes resolving. 321.1 354.2 354.3 That pending unit keeps the chain active, so you keep control of the battlefield and may choose it for the unit's return. 323.5 330 331.1 355.2.a A token unit instead ceases to exist immediately after moving to banishment, before Arcane Shift can instruct its owner to play it again. 186.1 Steps Arcane Shift banishes the unit, causing a cleanup. 319.6 Arcane Shift then instructs the unit's owner to play it, moving the unit to the chain as a pending item before the spell finishes resolving. 354.2 354.3 420.3 Cleanup runs while the unit remains pending, so the active chain prevents you from losing control of the empty battlefield. 321.1 323.5 330 331.1 354.4 During finalization, you choose the still-controlled battlefield as the unit's location. 355.2.a The unit then enters there. 359.2.c

rulings.question: When exactly does Astral Heron trigger, and which card gets its discount?
rulings.answer: Astral Heron triggers after your first card to finish resolving each turn, provided Astral Heron is at a battlefield then. If its triggered ability resolves, it discounts the next card you play this turn after that resolution. In a trigger condition, "When you play" is checked only when the act of playing that card is completed by its resolution. 420.4.a If a spell is countered instead of resolving, it does not trigger Astral Heron, and the first card you later resolve that turn can trigger it instead. 420.4.a.1 When the condition is fulfilled, the triggered ability is placed on the chain and must resolve before the discount exists. 383.3 407.5 391.4 Once it resolves, "the next card you play this turn" means the next card you place on the chain and queue for finalization. 420.5 Astral Heron's discount is applied while determining that card's total cost, before you pay the cost and finish finalizing it. 356.4 357

rulings.question: Does Astral Heron's ability trigger if it's the first card I play this turn and I play it to a battlefield?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Astral Heron is your first card played that turn and enters a battlefield as it resolves. A unit resolves immediately after finalizing. 337.2 During that resolution, it enters the board at its chosen location. 359.2.c Only after Astral Heron finishes resolving is it considered played for trigger conditions. 420.4.a Triggered abilities of permanents can have their conditions evaluated while their source is on the board. 384.2 Astral Heron is therefore at the battlefield when the game evaluates its trigger condition after the completed play. 383.2.c The immediately following "if I'm at a battlefield" is part of the trigger condition and is checked at that time. 383.2.a 383.2.a.1

rulings.question: Does Astral Heron trigger if the first card I play moves Astral Heron to base?
rulings.answer: No, if the spell leaves Astral Heron at base when it finishes resolving. A card is not considered played, and abilities that trigger from playing it are not evaluated, until that card finishes resolving. 350.1 420.4.a Astral Heron's trigger condition is therefore checked only after the spell's movement instructions have been completed. 383.2.c Because "if I'm at a battlefield" is part of that trigger condition, the ability is not placed on the chain if Astral Heron is at base by then. 383.2.a.1 This differs from moving Astral Heron after its triggered ability has already been placed on the chain, when the condition has already been satisfied. 383.2.a.1

rulings.question: Once Astral Heron's triggered ability is on the chain, can I stop the cost reduction by killing or moving Astral Heron?
rulings.answer: No. Once the triggered ability is on the chain, it still creates the discount even if you kill or move Astral Heron. "If I'm at a battlefield" is part of the trigger condition, so it is not checked again when the ability resolves. 383.2.a.1 The effect does not need Astral Heron's location or continued presence. When the triggered ability resolves, it creates a delayed ability that is not associated with Astral Heron and remains applicable at its specified time even if Astral Heron has left the board. 391.4 393

rulings.question: If the spell that receives Astral Heron's discount is later countered, is the discount granted to a different card instead?
rulings.answer: No. Once the discount has reduced the next spell's cost, countering that spell does not transfer the discount to another card. Astral Heron's triggered ability creates a delayed passive ability that applies only during the specified window for "the next card you play this turn." 391.4 392 The discount applies while determining that card's total cost, and the reduced cost is then paid before the card finishes finalizing. 356.4 357 By the time the finalized spell can be countered, that specified window has ended. 359.3.c

rulings.question: If Azir, Sovereign is killed or returned to his base before his attack trigger resolves, do token units still move?
rulings.answer: If Azir is killed, no token units move; if he is returned to base, no token units move unless he returns to a battlefield before the move instruction executes. Removing Azir does not by itself stop the triggered ability from resolving. 407.2 407.5 "This battlefield" refers to information drawn from Azir as the ability's source. 359.3.f.1 Because Azir's effect does not specify another time, the game checks that information when the instruction executes. 359.3.f.2 If Azir is at base or no longer on the board then, he has no battlefield for the instruction to use, so the move instruction is ignored and no token units move. 359.3.e.12 A recalled Azir remains the same permanent on the board, so returning him to a battlefield before execution supplies a battlefield for the instruction. 457 124 A killed Azir moves from the board to the trash. 429.2 That card becomes a new object for tracking. 124 Returning it to the board therefore does not restore the source tracked by the ability.

rulings.question: Can my opponent react before Baited Hook kills my unit?
rulings.answer: Yes. "Kill a friendly unit" comes after the ":" in Baited Hook's activated ability, so it is an effect instruction rather than part of the activation cost. 377.1 That instruction targets a friendly unit, and you choose that target while the ability is being finalized. 355.10 403.2 After Baited Hook's ability is finalized, opponents have an opportunity to play Reactions before it resolves and kills the target. 407.4 The later might limit refers to the unit affected by the kill, so these are linked instructions. 359.3.e.14 After the unit enters the trash, Baited Hook uses its might from immediately before that zone change. 359.3.e.13 Example You activate Baited Hook, targeting a friendly unit with 4 . In response, your opponent plays Stupefy . As the newer chain item, Stupefy resolves first and gives the unit -1 , so it has 3 when Baited Hook kills it. 340.1 Baited Hook therefore lets you banish a unit with up to 4 from among the top 5 cards of your main deck.

rulings.question: What happens if the targeted unit is removed before Baited Hook's ability resolves?
rulings.answer: The unit is not killed, you still look at the top 5 cards, but you cannot banish or play a unit from among them and must recycle every card you looked at. If the friendly unit is no longer a legal target when the ability resolves, it is unaffected and the kill instruction is ignored. 359.3.e.2 359.3.e.5 Its might is then null, so the instructions that would use that might to banish and play a unit are ignored. 359.3.e.12 The independent instruction to recycle the rest still happens, and no card was banished, so every card you looked at is recycled. 359.3.e.5

rulings.question: If Mordekaiser, Twice Slain replaces Baited Hook's kill, can I still banish and play a unit?
rulings.answer: No. You still look at the top 5 cards of your main deck, but you cannot banish or play a unit from among them and must recycle every card you looked at. When Mordekaiser, Twice Slain replaces his death, Baited Hook's kill action does not occur. 370.1.a.1 The banish instruction directly references that action through "the killed unit," so it is ignored when the kill is negated. 359.3.e.6 359.3.e.14 359.3.e.14.b The separate instruction to "play it" is also ignored because the banish instruction it refers to was ignored. 135.2.b.5 359.3.e.14.a The independent instruction to look at the top 5 cards still executes because it does not refer to the negated kill. 359.3.e.14.b The recycle instruction refers to the cards you looked at rather than the kill, so it also executes. 359.3.e.14 359.3.e.14.a Because none was banished, every card you looked at is "the rest" and is recycled.

rulings.question: Does a unit's Deathknell resolve before or after the unit played by Baited Hook and its triggers?
rulings.answer: The unit played by Baited Hook enters before the killed unit's [Deathknell] resolves. Abilities triggered by playing that unit also resolve before the [Deathknell]. Finalizing first does not mean resolving first: pending items finalize in the order they were added to the chain, 337.1.b but the newest finalized item resolves first. 340.1 Baited Hook kills the unit and adds its [Deathknell] as a pending item, then starts playing the chosen unit and adds it after the [Deathknell]. 808.1.d.2 354.2 The [Deathknell] finalizes first and waits on the chain. The chosen unit finalizes next and enters immediately, adding any abilities triggered by playing it above the [Deathknell]. 337.2 359.2.c 383.2.c 383.3 383.4.a.2 The newer triggered abilities resolve first, followed by the older [Deathknell].

rulings.question: If Baited Hook kills Glasc Mixologist and plays Karthus, Eternal, does Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell trigger twice?
rulings.answer: No. Baited Hook kills Glasc Mixologist before it plays Karthus, Eternal . Glasc's [Deathknell] triggers before he enters the trash. 808.1.d.2 Karthus's passive ability is active only while he is on the board. 365.1 Karthus entering later does not reevaluate Glasc's earlier death or make the [Deathknell] trigger again. 383.2.c.3 Glasc's [Deathknell] can play only one unit from the trash.

rulings.question: Does Baron Nashor move to the Baron Pit when it's created as part of playing him?
rulings.answer: No. Baron Nashor enters the Baron Pit directly; he does not move there. Moving means changing position between spaces on the board, while entering the board from another zone is a zone change. 448.1 448.2 When Baron Nashor creates the Baron Pit, his replacement effect changes his entry location from the originally chosen location to the Baron Pit. 369.3

rulings.question: Can Hunters' Circle reduce Baron Nashor's cost when he creates the Baron Pit?
rulings.answer: Yes, if you choose Hunters' Circle as Baron Nashor's play location and he is the first unit or gear you play there on your turn; Hunters' Circle reduces his cost by even though he enters the Baron Pit instead. A unit's play location is chosen before its cost is determined, so Hunters' Circle's discount applies. 355.2 356.4 Baron Nashor's replacement effect later changes only where he enters. 369.3 It does not change his chosen play location. 355.15 His cost has already been determined and paid by then, so it is not recalculated. 356 357 359.2.c

rulings.question: Does The Exile make Baron Nashor enter a newly created Baron Pit ready?
rulings.answer: If you control The Exile and choose a battlefield you control as Baron Nashor's play location, Baron Nashor enters the newly created Baron Pit ready regardless of which replacement effect applies first. The Exile checks the battlefield Baron Nashor was played to, not the battlefield where he enters. The chosen battlefield remains his play location when his replacement effect changes his entry location to the Baron Pit. 355.2 355.15 369.3 One replacement effect changes the entry location, and the other makes Baron Nashor enter ready. Applying either one first leaves the other applicable to Baron Nashor's modified entry. 370.1 370.2 The effects can be applied in either order. 372 Both orders therefore produce the same result.

rulings.question: What happens after Baron Nashor enters the Baron Pit?
rulings.answer: Baron Nashor's entry contests the newly created Baron Pit and leads to a non-combat showdown there. The Baron Pit remains uncontrolled until that showdown closes. Entry and Showdown Opening The Baron Pit is created uncontrolled. 440.4.b Baron Nashor enters it and contests it for his controller. 190.3.a.1 His entry causes a cleanup, which stages a showdown at the Baron Pit. 319.6 316.8.b That showdown normally begins during the cleanup. If multiple showdowns are ready to begin, the turn player chooses which one begins. 323.11 The Baron Pit remains uncontrolled while the showdown is ongoing. 190.4.b Closing and Conquest The showdown closes after every player passes focus in sequence without playing a card or activating an ability. 347.2.a 348 If Baron Nashor's controller is then the only player with units there, they establish control of the Baron Pit and conquer it if they have not scored it that turn. 348.2.a 348.2.a.1

rulings.question: After Baron Nashor creates the Baron Pit, does it need to be scored to win by conquering?
rulings.answer: Yes, when the potential winning point would come from conquering. At match point, a player gains the final point from a conquer only if they have scored every battlefield on the board that turn, including the Baron Pit . 473.1.b 473.1.b.1 If they have not scored every battlefield, they draw a card instead. 473.1.b.1

rulings.question: Can a unit survive combat damage that becomes lethal when Baron Nashor dies in the same combat?
rulings.answer: Yes, if the unit does not have lethal damage when the cleanup checks it while Baron Nashor's +2 still applies. The cleanup checks all units for lethal damage only once, so a unit that becomes lethal after Baron Nashor leaves is not checked again during that cleanup. 323.4 Steps Suppose Baron Nashor is assigned lethal combat damage and a friendly Evelynn, Entrancing is assigned 2 combat damage. Lethal-damage check: Baron Nashor has lethal damage, while Evelynn's 2 marked damage is less than her current 4 : her printed 2 plus Baron Nashor's +2 . 142.4.b Of the two, only Baron Nashor has lethal damage during the check, so the cleanup kills him and not Evelynn. 323.4 Baron Nashor's passive ability stops applying when he leaves the board. 365.1 Evelynn therefore returns to 2 after the lethal-damage check has finished. Her 2 marked damage is now lethal. 142.4.b That cleanup does not check her again. Combat healing: The combat special cleanup heals all units, clearing Evelynn's marked damage. 468.1.a.1 Baron Nashor's departure causes another cleanup. 319.6 322 Evelynn has no marked damage when that cleanup checks for lethal damage, so she is not killed. 323.4

rulings.question: Can I play Baron Nashor while an opponent's Mageseeker Warden is at a battlefield?
rulings.answer: Yes. You choose your base as Baron Nashor's play location because Mageseeker Warden makes it the only legal option. 355.2 355.2.a If the Baron Pit is not on the board, Baron Nashor's "as you play me" instruction adds it and his replacement effect changes his entry from your chosen base to the Baron Pit. 135.2.b.3 369.3 If the Baron Pit is already on the board, Baron Nashor does not add it, so the conditional replacement does not apply and he enters your chosen base. 359.2.c 369.3

rulings.question: Can Bedeviling Stranger's play effect target any battlefield?
rulings.answer: When Bedeviling Stranger is played from face down, its play effect can choose only the battlefield it was played to and a legal enemy unit there; when played from anywhere else, it can choose any battlefield containing an enemy unit it can legally target. The play effect has two targets: the battlefield it tells you to choose and the enemy unit mentioned in its later return instruction. 355.10 You choose both targets while the ability finalizes, even though you decide whether to return the enemy unit later during resolution. 383.3.a.3 403.2 When a permanent with [Hidden] is played from face down, each target of its play effect must be chosen from options at the battlefield that permanent was played to unless the ability's own targeting restriction makes this impossible. 811.1.d.3 A battlefield is itself a game object at its own location, so only the battlefield where Bedeviling Stranger was played satisfies this restriction. 199.1 If no legal enemy unit is there, the pending play effect is removed from the chain without finalizing. 403.4 This targeting restriction applies only when a card is played from face down. 811.1.d Playing Bedeviling Stranger from your hand, or from your trash through Last Rites or Endless Riches , therefore lets you choose any battlefield with a legal enemy unit there.

rulings.question: Does Bedeviling Stranger check for four units during finalization or resolution?
rulings.answer: Bedeviling Stranger checks for four or more units at the chosen battlefield only when its ability resolves, not during finalization. You choose both the battlefield and an enemy unit there as targets during finalization, even if fewer than four units are there then. 355.10 403.2 The later "if there are 4 or more units there" clause is part of the effect because it does not immediately follow the "When you play me" trigger condition. 383.2.a.1 383.2.b An instruction with no other stated timing executes during resolution. 135.2.b.3 After the ability finalizes on the chain, players can play cards and abilities with [Reaction] before it resolves. 407.4 When the ability resolves, it rechecks whether the same targets still meet every targeting restriction. 359.3.e.2 359.3.e.2.a 407.5 If those responses leave fewer than four units at the chosen battlefield, the ability still resolves, but its return instruction does not execute. 135.2.b.5.b 407.5

rulings.question: If I play Bedeviling Stranger from face down, does its play effect still work if it leaves the board in response?
rulings.answer: If Bedeviling Stranger was played from face down and leaves the board after its play effect finalizes but before it resolves, the effect still resolves, but both targets become illegal because the missing source cannot identify the battlefield required by [Hidden], so its return instruction is ignored. 359.3.e.5 359.3.e.6 407.5 811.1.d.3.a The finalized ability remains on the chain after its source leaves. 407.2 The target choices themselves do not change. 355.15 Instead, the ability rechecks whether those targets still satisfy every targeting restriction, including restrictions imposed by other effects. 359.3.e.2 359.3.e.2.a Both targets depend on the battlefield information supplied by Bedeviling Stranger as the source of an effect restricted by [Hidden]. 811.1.d.3 811.1.d.3.a An opponent can create this outcome by responding to the finalized play effect with Gust or Star-Crossed . 407.4 The newer spell resolves first and returns Bedeviling Stranger to its owner's hand, so the play effect resolves afterward without returning an enemy unit. 340.1

rulings.question: Can Bone Skewer choose a unit that says it "can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities"?
rulings.answer: Yes. The unit's untargetability ability is inactive while the card is in hand, and Bone Skewer's choice does not target it. "I can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities" is a passive untargetability ability. 757 757.1 Passive abilities of permanents are typically active only while they are on the board. 365.1 An ability that functions in another zone describes that context itself, 366.1 which this ability does not, so it has no effect in hand. Separately, a card in hand is not a target because the hand is not a public zone. 355.10.a

rulings.question: Does Bone Skewer stun a unit that can't be chosen by enemy spells or abilities?
rulings.answer: Yes. The reflexive trigger that stuns the unit does not ask its controller to choose anything. If the opponent plays the unit, Bone Skewer's "then do this" wording creates a reflexive trigger. 388.1 388.2 The trigger is linked to the preceding ability, and "it" can only refer to the unit played by that ability. 395.1 398 The unit is therefore programmatically determined rather than chosen by the trigger's controller, so it is not a target. 355.10.d 355.10.d.1 Untargetability does not prevent the stun because it only prevents the unit from being a legal target. 758

rulings.question: If a unit chosen by Bone Skewer has Hidden, can the opponent hide it instead of playing it?
rulings.answer: No. Hide is a separate action, not a way to fulfill Bone Skewer's instruction to play the unit. 811.1.c.1 Bone Skewer instructs the opponent to play the unit as a limited action, following the normal play process except where the effect says otherwise. 420.3 420.3.b

rulings.question: Can a unit played for free by Bone Skewer still get an effect for paying an optional additional cost?
rulings.answer: Yes. The phrase "any and all costs" in Bone Skewer's text is broader than the standard "ignoring its cost" wording. Standard cost-ignoring only zeroes out a card's base energy and power costs. 356.1.b.1 The opponent chooses whether to pay an optional additional cost while making the relevant choices for the unit. 355.1.a A chosen additional cost is included when determining the unit's total cost, which Bone Skewer then sets to zero. 356.2 356.5.a The optional additional cost counts as paid based on that decision, regardless of the amount actually spent. 356.4.f.1 Example You play Bone Skewer and choose Nami, Headstrong from your opponent's hand. Your opponent chooses to pay Nami's optional additional cost of , and Bone Skewer sets the resulting total cost to zero. When Nami completes being played, her play effect triggers because the additional cost counts as paid, allowing your opponent to stun an enemy unit. 420.4.a

rulings.question: Does Brynhir Thundersong stop cards already on the chain?
rulings.answer: No. A card already on the chain has already started its play because playing a card means placing it there and queuing it for finalization. 420.1 Once Brynhir Thundersong's play effect resolves, it prevents opponents from starting further plays that turn, but it does not stop cards already on the chain from finalizing or resolving. If one of those cards later instructs an opponent to play another card, Brynhir can still make the new play impossible without preventing that card from finalizing. 358.3.a The play instruction is negated, so the second card stays in its current zone. 359.3.e.6 The card already on the chain continues resolving and does as much as it can. 055

rulings.question: Can I choose a unit's current battlefield as Call to Battle's destination?
rulings.answer: No. When a spell or ability has you choose a move destination, that destination must be somewhere other than the unit's current location. 355.4 355.4.a Call to Battle has you choose both the unit and the battlefield, so the chosen battlefield cannot be the unit's current location.

rulings.question: Does Cataclysm still move a unit if the chosen battlefield is unoccupied when it resolves?
rulings.answer: No, if the chosen battlefield is unoccupied when Cataclysm resolves, the chosen unit does not move. Cataclysm requires the move's destination to be "an occupied enemy battlefield," and a move's source defines any restrictions on its legal destinations. 451.1 You choose the destination while playing the spell and cannot change that choice later unless a spell or ability instructs you to. 355.4 355.15 Once the chosen battlefield is unoccupied, it no longer satisfies Cataclysm's destination restriction, so the move cannot occur. The battlefield is a restriction on the move's destination, not a target. 355.10.b Cataclysm therefore does not mistarget solely because the battlefield becomes unoccupied. Its move instruction is instead impossible and negated. 359.3.e.6

rulings.question: In what order does Chronobreak play unit cards with different owners?
rulings.answer: The turn player begins playing the units they own, choosing their order. Each other player then does the same in turn order. 303.2.a Those units wait on the chain until Chronobreak finishes resolving, then process in that order: 354.2 354.3 The first unit card put on the chain undergoes finalization first. 337.1.b A unit that finalizes resolves immediately and enters before the next unit card undergoes finalization. 337.2 Any play effect that unit triggers is added after every unit already waiting on the chain. 383.4.a.2 The remaining unit cards undergo finalization in the order they were put on the chain. 337.1.b Any ordinary play effects then finalize oldest-first in the order they were added. 337.1.b 383.4.a.2

rulings.question: Can Chronobreak play back a unit token?
rulings.answer: No. The unit token ceases to exist immediately after Chronobreak banishes it, so it no longer exists when Chronobreak would instruct its owner to play it. 186 186.1

rulings.question: When I play Consuming Curse from my trash, does it count itself for the bonus damage?
rulings.answer: No. The first step of playing Consuming Curse moves it from your trash to the chain. 354 Its damage instruction executes before it returns to your trash. 359.3.d Only other cards named Consuming Curse that remain in your trash add bonus damage.

rulings.question: Does Diana, Lunari's ability resolve before or after attack and defend abilities from the start of combat?
rulings.answer: When combat opens with a new showdown, Diana's ability triggers first but resolves last, after all attack and defend abilities generated immediately afterward. Start-of-showdown effects happen before units gain their attacker and defender designations, so Diana triggers before those designations trigger attack and defend abilities. 383.4.e 383.4.f 466.2.a 466.2.b 466.2.c.3 These are consecutive combat-opening tasks with no priority between them, so all resulting abilities are pending on the combat chain before any is finalized or can resolve. 334.1 334.2 466.2.d The newest chain items resolve first, so the attack and defend abilities resolve before Diana's ability. 340.1 If combat opens during an existing showdown, the showdown does not begin again, so Diana's "when a showdown begins here" ability does not trigger. 466.1 466.2

rulings.question: When do I pay the 1 energy for Diana, Lunari's ability?
rulings.answer: You pay it while Diana's triggered ability is being finalized, before opponents receive the normal opportunity to play Reactions to the ability. 407.4 Because "you may" is the first part of the effect, you choose whether to perform the ability during finalization. 383.3.a The immediately following "pay to [Predict]" is a cost within instructions, so the payment becomes the triggered ability's base cost and must be paid for the ability to finalize. 383.3.b 383.3.b.1 740.4.a While paying, you may activate an eligible [Add] ability with [Reaction] to provide the energy. 445.2.c If you decline to pay, the pending ability is removed from the chain without finalizing. 405.2 If you pay, it becomes a finalized chain item, and opponents may react before it resolves. 407.2 407.4 When it resolves, you [Predict], reveal the top card of your main deck, and draw that card if it is a spell. Errata Diana received functional errata. Older printings say "you may pay . If you do, ..."; her current text says "you may pay to ..." instead. This changes the payment from an instruction performed during resolution into a cost paid while finalizing the ability.

rulings.question: Can I decline to play the card chosen from those revealed by Drakehound Packmaster?
rulings.answer: Drakehound Packmaster requires you to attempt to play the chosen card: you may stop the play by declining a positive energy or power payment, 445.2 but you cannot decline a zero resource cost 445.1.b or a non-standard additional cost that is mandatory or that you chose, 445.1.a 356.2.a.1 356.2.b.1 and if such a non-standard cost cannot be paid, the play fails instead. 203.3 358.2 Declining the resource payment or failing to pay a required cost undoes the play and returns the card to its owner's banishment. 056.2 354 445.2.a 358.5 The instruction to play the card is not optional, so you carry it out as far as possible using the normal play process. 055 420.3 420.3.b Drakehound Packmaster sets the card's base energy and power costs to zero, but mandatory additional costs, optional additional costs you choose, and cost increases still apply. 356.1.b.1 356.1.b.3 356.2 356.3 You choose whether to pay an optional additional cost before the total cost is determined. 355.1.a Zero resource cost If the card's total energy and power cost is zero, that cost is paid without performing the Pay game action and cannot be declined. 445.1.b Zero therefore gives you no way to cancel the play during finalization. Positive resource cost If the total includes a positive energy or power cost, you may choose not to pay those resources. 445.2 This applies whether the resource cost came from a mandatory additional cost or an optional additional cost you chose. 356.2.a.1 356.2.b.1 Declining does not remove only that additional cost; it undoes the entire play. 445.2.a Non-standard costs The choice to decline the Pay game action applies only to energy and power. 445.1.a A mandatory non-standard additional cost, or an optional non-standard additional cost you chose, must be paid if possible. 356.2.a.1 356.2.b.1 357.2 You may omit an optional cost when making that earlier choice, but after choosing it, you cannot decline it during payment. 355.1.a 355.15 If the required game action is impossible, the cost cannot be paid. 203.3 The card then fails its cost check, its play is undone, and it returns to its owner's banishment. 358.2 358.5 If the total contains both a positive resource cost and a non-standard cost, you may decline the resource payment before performing the non-standard cost because energy and power are paid first. 357.1 357.2 445.2 Examples of cards with mandatory non-standard additional costs include Cruel Patron , Sacrifice , and Ekko, Ingenious .

rulings.question: If a unit survives Boy Who Shattered Time's end-of-turn kill, will it die on a later turn?
rulings.answer: Under the official Radiance ruling , a unit whose death is replaced, for example by Unlicensed Armory or by Mordekaiser, Twice Slain replacing his own death, will not try to kill itself again on a later turn. Boy Who Shattered Time grants the unit "Kill me at end of turn." The rules treat "at end of turn" and "at the end of this turn" as synonymous, so its trigger condition occurs only during the current turn's Ending Step. 359.3.e.16 When that ability resolves, either replacement causes its kill not to happen. 370.1.a.1 370.1.b The triggered ability still finishes resolving. 407.5 Its specified time has then passed, so it cannot trigger again on a later turn. 391.2 392

rulings.question: Does a unit affected by Boy Who Shattered Time still die if it is banished and played again?
rulings.answer: No. If it is banished and played again before the ability triggers, the returned card is a new unit without the granted kill ability. Moving from the board to banishment makes the card a new object, 124 and its temporary modifications, including the granted ability, cease to be tracked. 124.1 A legally timed effect can also banish and replay it after the kill ability is already on the chain. The ability remains on the chain, but "me" refers to its original source, not the returned card, which is a new unit. 359.3.f.1 359.3.f.2 407.2 407.5 Ekko, Revolutionary 's [Action] ability and Chronobreak can use the first timing window, before the kill ability triggers. Neither can be used in response once the ability is on the chain because neither has [Reaction]. 309.1.a By contrast, Temporal Breach can respond to the kill ability if it was played from face down after gaining [Reaction]. 811.1.b

rulings.question: How does Elder Dragon affect combat damage assignment?
rulings.answer: While you control Elder Dragon on the board, 1 combat damage from your units is lethal to an enemy unit regardless of its might, unless another effect changes how much must be assigned or prevents that damage. Elder Dragon changes the lethal-damage value for enemy units with its controller's damage, and the smallest valid amount of damage is 1. 142.3.b 142.4.c 418.1.e You must assign lethal damage to one unit before assigning damage to another, and you cannot assign more than the lethal minimum while another unit remains. 467.2.c.3 467.2.c.4 With Elder Dragon, that normally means assigning exactly 1 damage to an enemy unit before moving to the next. Passive abilities and replacement effects, including prevention, are considered during assignment and can change this minimum. 467.2.c.4.a 467.2.c.5 Elder Dragon vs. Imperial Decree Suppose Pakaa Cub , with 3 , is your only attacker against three undamaged copies of Noxus Hopeful , each defending with 4 . With Elder Dragon, you assign 1 damage from Pakaa Cub to each Noxus Hopeful, and all three are killed during the combat cleanup. 323.4 467.2.d 468.1.a Imperial Decree does not change lethal damage or combat damage assignment. Assigning damage is not dealing damage, so its delayed triggered ability triggers only after a unit actually takes damage and then attempts to kill that unit. 383.2.c 391.2 467.2.c.1 With Imperial Decree instead, Pakaa Cub still assigns all 3 damage, but you cannot split it among the three Noxus Hopefuls. You must assign lethal damage to one before moving to another, so all 3 damage is assigned to the Noxus Hopeful you choose first. Of the three Noxus Hopefuls, only that one takes Pakaa Cub's combat damage, so Imperial Decree's kill ability triggers for it and not the other two.

rulings.question: Does damage from earlier in the turn become lethal when Elder Dragon enters, and can I react?
rulings.answer: Damage still marked by Elder Dragon's controller becomes lethal to enemy units when Elder Dragon enters, and opponents cannot react after it enters before the resulting cleanup handles that lethal damage. Elder Dragon's "your damage" means damage marked by its controller. 142.3.b Its first ability is a passive statement that changes the lethal-damage value for those enemy units while Elder Dragon is on the board. 142.4.c 364.2 365.1 Finalizing a unit does not pass priority, and the unit resolves immediately. 337.1.a 337.2 After Elder Dragon enters, a cleanup happens without passing or awarding priority, and every unit with lethal damage is killed unless that death is replaced. 319.6 320.1 323.4 370.1 370.1.c Elder Dragon's separate "When you play me" ability is a triggered play effect, but it does not create a response window before this lethal-damage check. 383.4.a 383.4.a.2 Example You play Flurry of Blades during your turn, and its 1 damage remains marked on enemy units at battlefields. When you later play Elder Dragon directly, each of those units is killed in the cleanup caused by Elder Dragon entering before your opponents can react. The same result occurs if Dazzling Aurora plays Elder Dragon at the end of your turn. End-of-turn abilities happen in the Ending Step, before the Expiration Step's special cleanup heals all units, so reaching the end of the turn has not itself healed Flurry of Blades' damage yet. 317.1.a 317.2.a 317.2.b Opponents may react while Dazzling Aurora's triggered ability waits to resolve. 383.1 337.4 338.1.a.2 Once that ability begins resolving and reveals Elder Dragon, no new priority window opens before Elder Dragon enters and the affected units are killed.

rulings.question: Can Elder Dragon target a unit after Zhonya's Hourglass recalls it?
rulings.answer: Yes, if you play Elder Dragon while an enemy unit at a battlefield has your damage marked on it and that unit's controller controls Zhonya's Hourglass in their base: Zhonya's Hourglass replaces that unit's death and recalls it before you choose targets for Elder Dragon's play effect, so you can choose the recalled unit in its controller's base. If another valid enemy unit remains at a battlefield, you can choose that unit as well because it is at a different location. Elder Dragon enters, and its passive makes your marked damage lethal to the damaged enemy unit. 142.4.c Its play effect is then added to the chain as a pending item. 383.4.a.2 Both Elder Dragon entering and its play effect being added require cleanup before play continues. 319.6 319.3 All outstanding cleanups finish before the pending effect can begin finalization. 320 334.2 During cleanup, the damaged unit would be killed. 323.4 Zhonya's Hourglass replaces that death: the Hourglass is killed instead, and the unit is healed, exhausted, and recalled to its controller's base rather than killed. 370.1.a.1 Killing Zhonya's Hourglass sends it from the board to the trash, making another cleanup outstanding after the current one. 429.1 319.6 322 After all cleanups finish, you choose targets while finalizing the play effect. 334.2 337.1 191.5.c 403.2 The recalled unit is now in base, and any valid enemy unit that remains at a battlefield is at a different location, so both can be chosen. 146.1 198.1 355.11.a When the effect resolves, it deals 1 to each target it affects, marking damage on each unit separately. 418.1.b 418.1.c If Elder Dragon remains on the board, its passive makes that damage lethal, so each affected unit would be killed during the cleanup after the ability leaves the chain. 142.3.b 142.4.c 365.1 407.5 319.5 323.4

rulings.question: Does Elder Dragon's play effect finalize if its passive leaves no enemy units to target?
rulings.answer: Yes. The words "up to" allow Elder Dragon's controller to choose zero targets. 355.13 Because the ability does not begin with "you may," its controller cannot decline to perform it, so the play effect finalizes even when no enemy units remain. 383.3.a 403.4 407.2 After Elder Dragon enters, its play effect is added to the chain before the resulting cleanup. 319.6 334.2.a 383.4.a.2 Elder Dragon's passive ability makes its controller's marked damage on enemy units lethal, so that cleanup may kill an opponent's last units. 142.4.c 323.4 The pending play effect remains on the chain throughout the cleanup, so the opponent retains control of their empty battlefields and their [Hidden] cards remain there. 320 323.5 323.6.a 330 331.1 After the play effect finalizes with zero targets, the opponent may play an eligible card from face down as a [Reaction] before the effect resolves. 407.4 When the effect resolves with no targets, it simply does nothing.

rulings.question: What happens if I play Elnuk Herd from face down to a battlefield with no other friendly units?
rulings.answer: Elnuk Herd is the only legal target of its play effect, so it gets +3 this turn and then recycles itself. The play effect is added to the chain only after Elnuk Herd enters the battlefield. 383.4.a.2 Its current text says "a friendly unit," so the ability can target Elnuk Herd itself because an ability and its source are separate objects. 355.9.c 355.10 Because Elnuk Herd was played from face down, the play effect must choose a target at that battlefield. 811.1.d.3 With no other friendly unit there, Elnuk Herd must be chosen during finalization. 403.2 403.4.b When the ability resolves, it gives Elnuk Herd +3 before recycling it because Elnuk Herd was played from face down. Errata Elnuk Herd received functional errata. Older printings say "another friendly unit"; the current text says "a friendly unit." Removing "another" allows Elnuk Herd to target itself.

rulings.question: When do I pay 1 energy and return a unit for Emperor's Dais?
rulings.answer: During finalization, you decide whether to use the ability 383.3.a and, if you do, pay and return the unit. 383.3.b 383.3.b.1 Both actions form one inseparable base cost, so you must complete them together for the ability to finalize. 740.4.a The pending ability is removed without finalizing if no legal unit can be chosen 403.4 or if you decline the complete cost. 405.2 While paying the energy, you may activate an eligible [Add] ability with [Reaction] to provide it. 445.2.c The unit you return is part of the cost rather than a target, and it returns to its owner's hand during finalization. 355.10.c 355.10.c.1 If you have paid the cost, the ability finalizes and opponents may then react before it resolves. 407.2 407.4 Errata Emperor's Dais received functional errata. Older printings connect the Sand Soldier instruction with "If you do, play"; the current text uses "to play" instead. This changes the energy payment and unit return from instructions performed during resolution into one cost completed while finalizing the ability.

rulings.question: What happens if Emperor's Dais leaves before its ability resolves?
rulings.answer: A battlefield token that replaces Emperor's Dais still supplies the "here" location for its Sand Soldier, but if Emperor's Dais leaves without replacement, the Sand Soldier cannot be played because "here" no longer identifies a location. The replacing token is treated as the same game object as Emperor's Dais. 439.1.a Without a replacement, Emperor's Dais has no location when "here" is checked as the instruction executes. 359.3.e.12 359.3.f.1 359.3.f.2

rulings.question: Does The Exile make the Sand Soldier from Emperor's Dais enter ready?
rulings.answer: Yes, with The Exile as your legend, the Sand Soldier unit token played by Emperor's Dais enters ready, even if you return your only unit there to pay the ability's cost. You establish control of Emperor's Dais before the conquest triggers its ability. 471.1 471.1.b 383.2.c The ability remains on the chain while the unit is returned and the Sand Soldier is played, so Emperor's Dais does not become uncontrolled in between. 309.1 323.5 407.5 The Sand Soldier is therefore played to a battlefield you control, so The Exile makes it enter ready.

rulings.question: How long does Endless Riches make me skip my Draw Phase?
rulings.answer: You skip every Draw Phase you would have for as long as Endless Riches remains on the board. "Skip your Draw Phase" is a passive ability and a replacement effect that replaces your Draw Phase with nothing. 364.2 444.1.a Passive abilities of permanents become active when the permanent enters the board and are typically active only while it remains there. 359.2.a 365.1 Once Endless Riches leaves the board, this ability is no longer active, so your later Draw Phases occur normally.

rulings.question: Can I hide cards from my trash while Endless Riches is on the board?
rulings.answer: No, Endless Riches does not allow you to hide cards from your trash. Endless Riches grants permission only to play cards from your trash. Hiding is a separate action from playing. 811.1.c.1 You can normally hide a card only from your hand or chosen champion zone. 811.1.b

rulings.question: Where does a spell played by Fizz, Trickster or Kai'Sa, Evolutionary go while Endless Riches is in play?
rulings.answer: Ordinarily, it is recycled to the bottom of its owner's main deck. 417.1 417.1.a 417.1.c The "then recycle it" text on Fizz, Trickster and Kai'Sa, Evolutionary creates a delayed replacement effect for a finalized spell leaving the chain other than through its own effect. 391.3.a Endless Riches creates another replacement effect that would replace the spell going to the trash with banishing it. 369.1 When both replacement effects apply to a spell that would go to the trash, the spell's controller chooses the order in which to apply them. 372 Either order recycles the spell. Fizz or Kai'Sa first: The spell is recycled instead of going to the trash, so Endless Riches no longer applies. Endless Riches first: The spell would be banished instead of going to the trash, but it is still leaving the chain, so the delayed replacement replaces that event with recycling it. 370.2 One boundary applies: if the spell's own effect instructs it to leave the chain during resolution, follow that instruction, except Endless Riches still banishes it if that instruction would put it in the trash. 391.3.a 369.1

rulings.question: Which costs does Ezreal, Prodigy reduce?
rulings.answer: Ezreal reduces only optional additional costs you choose to pay. These costs use both the word "may" and the exact phrase "as an additional cost." 356.2.b.1 [Accelerate] and [Repeat] are optional additional cost keywords, so Ezreal reduces them too. 805.1 820.1 Ezreal's discount applies to the optional additional cost itself as soon as that cost is added, and only to the chosen component, before discounts that apply to the card's total cost. 356.4.c 356.4.c.1 356.4.d Mandatory additional costs are not optional because they omit "may," so Ezreal does not reduce them. 356.2.a.1 Hard Bargain 's resource payment happens while carrying out its effect as the spell resolves. 158.1 It is not an additional cost to play Hard Bargain, so Ezreal does not reduce it. 204.2 205 Example Blast Corps Cadet says "You may pay as an additional cost to play me." Ezreal can reduce that optional additional cost to either or . By contrast, Ezreal does not reduce Cruel Patron 's mandatory cost to kill a friendly unit or the an opponent may pay during Hard Bargain's effect. Ezreal does reduce Hard Bargain's separate [Repeat] cost.

rulings.question: Does Fallen Feline stop a named spell already on the chain?
rulings.answer: No. A spell already on the chain has already started its play because playing a card means placing it there and queuing it for finalization. 420.1 While Fallen Feline is at a battlefield, it prevents opponents from starting another play of a spell with the chosen name, but it does not stop the spell already on the chain from finalizing or resolving. If that spell later instructs an opponent to play another spell with the chosen name, Fallen Feline can still make the new play impossible without preventing that spell from finalizing. 358.3.a The play instruction is negated, so the second spell stays in its current zone. 359.3.e.6 The spell already on the chain continues resolving and does as much as it can. 055

rulings.question: When can I react to Fallen Feline's play effect?
rulings.answer: You can react before its controller names a spell, but once the name is chosen, it is too late to start playing that spell while Fallen Feline remains at a battlefield. The name is chosen only when the play effect resolves, 355.18 after players have had the opportunity to react to the finalized ability. 407.4

rulings.question: Can Flash target a unit that is already in base?
rulings.answer: Yes, Flash can target a friendly unit that is already in base. 355.9.a 355.9.b 355.10 Flash specifies base as the destination instead of asking you to choose one, so the different-location restriction for player-chosen destinations does not make a unit already in base an illegal target. 002 355.4 355.4.a When Flash resolves, the unit cannot move because it would not change from one board space to another. 448.1

rulings.question: If Gangplank, Naval replaces one part of a spell or ability, does the rest still resolve?
rulings.answer: Yes, only the qualifying stun, might decrease, or return-to-hand event is replaced; the spell or ability's other instructions continue unless a later linked instruction specifically requires the replaced action to have occurred. 359.3.e.14.b A replacement effect only replaces the specific event or instruction that qualifies for it. 370.1 370.1.b Example You play Star-Crossed , targeting your own [Empowered] Gangplank as the friendly unit and an opponent's Elder Dragon as the enemy unit. Gangplank's replacement effect does not apply to the separate return event affecting Elder Dragon, so Elder Dragon returns to its owner's hand normally. Returning Gangplank is the qualifying event: instead of going to hand, he gets +3 this turn. The rest of Star-Crossed resolves normally; it simply produces a different result for the one return event involving Gangplank.

rulings.question: What happens when Switcheroo would reduce an Empowered Gangplank, Naval's might?
rulings.answer: When Switcheroo would decrease an [Empowered] Gangplank's might, Gangplank gets +3 this turn instead, while the increase affecting the other unit remains unchanged. Switcheroo chooses Gangplank when the spell is finalized. 355.5 355.10 When it resolves, Switcheroo first determines one difference, then creates separate might-increase and might-decrease effects for that fixed amount; replacing one does not recalculate or alter the other. 434.1.a 434.1.b 434.1.d Gangplank's replacement effect replaces the decrease affecting him because it comes from a spell that chose him, but an increase does not match any event his ability replaces and applies normally. 370.1 370.1.b Example An [Empowered] Gangplank with 6 is swapped with a Determined Sentry with 1 at the same battlefield via Switcheroo. The swap action calculates a difference of 5, then creates two effects: -5 for Gangplank and +5 for Determined Sentry. Gangplank's replacement effect replaces the -5 decrease affecting him with +3 this turn. The +5 effect applies only to Determined Sentry, so Gangplank's replacement effect does not affect it. After Switcheroo resolves, Gangplank has 9 , and Determined Sentry has 6 .

rulings.question: Can Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell target a unit that died from the same event?
rulings.answer: Yes, because Glasc's [Deathknell] chooses its target only after every unit killed by the same event has moved to its owner's trash; at that point, the target must be a unit card in your trash with an Energy cost no more than and a Power cost no more than . 403.2 429.2 The ability becomes pending before Glasc moves to the trash, but no target is chosen until the ability finalizes. 808.1.d.2 A killed token instead ceases to exist immediately after entering the trash, so it cannot be targeted. 186.1 During a cleanup, units with lethal damage are killed and moved to their owners' trashes before pending abilities can finalize. 323.4 320 334.2 When one effect instruction of a resolving spell or ability kills multiple units, their deaths are simultaneous. 370.1.a.2 No pending ability can finalize until the current spell or ability finishes resolving. 158.3

rulings.question: Can Glasc Mixologist's Deathknell play a unit to the battlefield where he died?
rulings.answer: Yes, as long as you controlled that battlefield when Glasc Mixologist died. Outside a showdown , Glasc's [Deathknell] is added as a pending item before he moves to the trash, and any cleanup already in progress or caused by his death finishes before that ability can finalize. 808.1.d.2 320 334.2 That pending ability keeps the chain in progress throughout the cleanup, so you do not lose control of the battlefield even if Glasc's death leaves it empty. 330 309.1 323.5 You can therefore choose that battlefield as a valid destination when the unit is finalized. 355.2.a During a showdown , control of the battlefield cannot change until instructed by the steps of the combat or showdown, so you can likewise choose that battlefield as the unit's destination. 190.4.b

rulings.question: What happens when Glasc Mixologist is my only defender and his Deathknell plays a unit where he died?
rulings.answer: The original combat result is determined only after Glasc's chosen unit enters and every associated chain item finishes. 468.2 At that point, the result depends on which players have units at the battlefield: Only your units remain: You win the original combat. 468.3.a Only your opponent's units remain: Your opponent wins the original combat. 468.3.a Both players have units there: Neither player wins, and a new showdown and combat are staged. 468.3.d 468.3.d.1 Neither player has units there: Neither player wins, and no new showdown or combat is staged. 468.3.d 468.3.d.1 Steps The combat cleanup heals all units before Glasc's pending [Deathknell] can be finalized. 468.1.a.1 320 334.2 Because Glasc was your only defender, no defenders remain during cleanup, so the surviving attackers are not recalled. 468.1.a.2 After the cleanup, Glasc's [Deathknell] resolves and begins playing the chosen unit. The unit becomes pending while the ability finishes. 354.2 354.3 The unit then finalizes and enters the battlefield exhausted. 359.2.c Any play effect and other resulting chain items also finish before combat result is determined. 383.4.a.2 468.2 The players' units then determine who won the original combat and whether a new showdown and combat are staged.

rulings.question: Can I play a unit from face down after Graves, Blasting Through's ability kills all my defenders?
rulings.answer: Yes, at your next legal opportunity, if the unit was hidden at that battlefield on an earlier turn and can otherwise be legally played. The cleanup after Graves's ability may kill your last defender, 323.4 but the ongoing combat prevents control of the battlefield from changing. 190.4.b You therefore still control the battlefield, and the facedown card stays there. 811.1.b 323.6.a The facedown unit can still be played. 811.6 Example Graves attacks alone, and his ability kills every defending unit. At your next legal opportunity, you play Evelynn, Entrancing from face down at that battlefield. Graves deals no combat damage, and Evelynn's 2 deals only 2 damage to the 4 Graves, so neither unit has lethal damage. 142.4.b 467.2.b 467.2.c 467.2.d Because Evelynn remains as a defender, Graves is recalled. 468.1.a.2 Evelynn's controller retains control, so Graves's controller does not conquer the battlefield. 468.3.d 468.5 471.1

rulings.question: Does an opponent pay Gravity Field's cost when I move their unit to its battlefield?
rulings.answer: No. The cost does not apply because you perform the move action, not the opponent who controls the unit. The player who performs a game action is responsible for it. 412.1 For example, Charm and Siren's Song each instruct you to move an enemy unit, so you are responsible even though your opponent controls that unit. Gravity Field's applied cost applies only when an opponent performs the move action to its battlefield. 204.4 204.4.a

rulings.question: Must an opponent pay Gravity Field's cost when an effect tells them to move a unit to its battlefield, or can they decline?
rulings.answer: They must pay to perform the move, but they may decline. If they decline or cannot pay, they move no unit. For example, Angler Wyrm and Call to Battle each instruct a chosen opponent to perform the move, so that opponent is responsible for it. 412.1 Gravity Field therefore applies its cost to that move action. 204.4 204.4.a Applied costs are paid as their associated game actions are performed. 204.4.b The word "must" does not remove the option to decline an applied cost. If the opponent declines or cannot pay, they cannot perform the move action. 204.4.c The move instruction is negated rather than ignored because it cannot be followed for a reason other than an illegal target or unavailable information. 359.3.e.6 407.5

rulings.question: If Heedless Resurrection is countered, is the killed unit returned?
rulings.answer: No. Killing a friendly unit is an additional cost paid while playing Heedless Resurrection. 356.7 357.2 Countering the spell later does not refund that cost, so the killed unit is not returned. 426.1.c 426.1.c.1

rulings.question: Can I kill a unit with Heedless Resurrection's cost and then resurrect that same unit?
rulings.answer: No. During the process of playing Heedless Resurrection, you choose a unit card already in your trash during step 2, while the friendly unit you intend to kill is still on the board. 355.5 355.8 355.9.a You pay the kill cost during step 4 of that process, after the target choice has been locked in. 357.2 355.15

rulings.question: Does Heedless Resurrection's "ignoring its cost" instruction also ignore the resurrected unit's additional costs, such as Accelerate?
rulings.answer: No. "Ignoring its cost" sets only the resurrected unit's base energy and power costs to zero; additional costs, such as [Accelerate], are applied afterward and are not waived. 356.1.b.1 356.1.b.3 805.2 If the resurrected unit has an optional additional cost you may choose whether to pay it; 356.2.b.1 if it has a mandatory additional cost you must pay it. 356.2.a.1

rulings.question: If Heedless Resurrection gains Repeat, do I need to kill a friendly unit for each repetition?
rulings.answer: No. Heedless Resurrection is played only once, so you pay its additional cost to kill a friendly unit only once. 357.2 820.3.a [Repeat] executes only the spell's resolution instructions again; instructions not performed on resolution, such as the additional-cost instruction, are not repeated. 820.1.d.1 820.1.d.2

rulings.question: If Hidden Blade's kill is prevented or replaced, does the target's controller draw?
rulings.answer: If Hidden Blade's target is legal when the spell begins resolving and remains on the board after the kill is prevented or replaced, its controller draws 2; if a replacement causes it to leave the board, no player draws. The phrase "its controller" links the draw to the unit affected by the preceding kill instruction. 359.3.e.14 If the legal target can't be killed, the kill instruction is negated rather than ignored. 359.3.e.6 Negating or replacing that kill does not stop the linked draw because the draw instruction does not refer to the kill action. 359.3.e.14.b The unit remains on the board: Hidden Blade can identify its controller, and that player draws 2. 359.3.e.12.a For example, Zhonya's Hourglass recalls the unit to base, where it remains on the board under its controller. The unit leaves the board: Hidden Blade can no longer identify a controller for that card, so no player draws. 359.3.e.12 For example, a unit previously affected by Smite is banished instead when Hidden Blade would kill it.

rulings.question: If Hidden Blade's target becomes illegal, does that target's controller draw?
rulings.answer: No. An illegal target is unaffected by Hidden Blade, so the kill instruction is ignored. 359.3.e.5 Hidden Blade's draw is linked to its kill instruction because "its controller" refers to the unit affected by that instruction. 359.3.e.14 When an earlier linked instruction is ignored, its later linked instructions are also ignored, so the controller does not draw. 359.3.e.14.a Example You play Hidden Blade targeting an opponent's unit at a battlefield. They respond by moving it to their base using Flash . Hidden Blade resolves. The unit is no longer at a battlefield, so it is an illegal target. The unit is not killed and the opponent does not draw.

rulings.question: If I target Irelia, Fervent with a spell or ability and it gets countered, does she still get +1 might?
rulings.answer: Yes, if you are Irelia's controller and choose her as the target; countering the original spell or ability does not counter her separate +1 ability. As Irelia's controller, you fulfill her trigger condition by choosing her while playing the original spell or ability. 412.1 412.4 355.5 355.7 400 After the original item finalizes, Irelia's triggered ability is added as a separate chain item. 383.4.b.2 383.4.b.3 Countering the original item afterward clears only that item, not Irelia's separate ability. 426.1.a

rulings.question: Does Blade Dancer's ability trigger Irelia, Fervent's +1 might?
rulings.answer: Blade Dancer 's ability can trigger Irelia once by readying an exhausted Irelia controlled by the same player, but it does not trigger her by choosing her. "It" in "ready it" automatically identifies the friendly unit from Blade Dancer's trigger condition instead of making another choice, so that unit is not a target of the ability. 355.10.d 355.10.d.1 Irelia's controller fulfills her trigger condition when Blade Dancer's ability changes her from exhausted to ready. 412.1 412.4 416.1 An already-ready Irelia cannot be readied again, so her ability does not trigger. 416.1.b 416.1.c

rulings.question: Does Irelia, Fervent get +1 might when she readies during the Awaken Phase?
rulings.answer: Yes, once, when her controller readies her from exhausted to ready during their Awaken Phase. During their Awaken Phase, Irelia's controller readies every game object they control that can be readied, and changing an exhausted Irelia to ready creates her trigger. 315.1.b 412.1 412.4 416.1 An already-ready Irelia cannot be readied again, so no readying event occurs and her ability does not trigger. 416.1.b 416.1.c

rulings.question: Does a Repeat spell targeting Irelia, Fervent for both instructions give her +1 might twice?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Irelia's controller chooses her both times; each choice is a separate targeting event, so Irelia triggers twice. Paying [Repeat] makes the spell execute its instructions an additional time, with choices made separately for each execution. 820.1.d 820.2 820.2.a Irelia's controller creates those two targeting events by choosing her once for each execution. 412.1 412.4 355.7 After the spell finalizes, one instance of Irelia's triggered ability is added as a pending item for each targeting event. 383.4.b.2 383.4.b.3 Example You control Irelia, play Feral Strength , and pay its [Repeat] cost, choosing her for both instructions. After Feral Strength finalizes, Irelia's ability triggers twice, once per targeting event, and both triggers are added to the chain. Irelia's two +1 modifiers and Feral Strength's two +2 modifiers give her +6 total this turn.

rulings.question: If Irresistible Faefolk moves to an uncontested, uncontrolled battlefield outside a showdown and pulls an enemy unit there, who is the attacker?
rulings.answer: Irresistible Faefolk's controller is the attacker. Irresistible Faefolk reaches the battlefield before its triggered ability can pull the enemy unit. 383.2.c It contests that battlefield for its controller because no one controls it and it was not already contested. 190.3.a.1 Its ability then pulls the enemy unit there. With opposing units now at the contested battlefield, the next cleanup marks it for combat. 319.8 323.8 When that combat begins, Irresistible Faefolk's controller is the attacker and the pulled unit's controller is the defender because Irresistible Faefolk was the unit that contested the battlefield. 466.2.c.1 466.2.c.2

rulings.question: If I play Irresistible Faefolk directly to a battlefield, does its ability trigger?
rulings.answer: No. A move is defined as a permanent changing its position from one location on the board to another. 448.1 When you play Irresistible Faefolk, it enters the board from a non-board zone (such as your hand), which is a zone change, not a move. 448.2

rulings.question: If an opponent responds to my move trigger by removing Irresistible Faefolk from the battlefield, does the enemy unit still move?
rulings.answer: Yes, removing Irresistible Faefolk by itself does not stop the enemy unit from moving. Removing Irresistible Faefolk is not a counter instruction. 426.1 426.2.a Its already-finalized ability remains on the chain and executes like a spell. 407.5 Irresistible Faefolk's trigger condition identifies the battlefield it moved to, so the ability records that battlefield when it triggers. 359.3.f.3 Removing Irresistible Faefolk later does not erase that destination, so the chosen enemy unit can still move there when the ability resolves.

rulings.question: Does Karthus, Eternal's ability apply if he dies from the same effect as the unit with Deathknell?
rulings.answer: Karthus applies to your other unit's [Deathknell] if the deaths are simultaneous or that unit is killed before Karthus. He doesn't apply if a separate kill action kills him first.
