When one kill action kills Karthus and another unit simultaneously, 370.1.a.2 as with The Ruination , the other unit's [Deathknell] is added before the kill instruction moves Karthus off the board. 429.1.a.1.b His passive ability is therefore still active and makes your [Deathknell] effect trigger an additional time. 365.1 If one effect instead performs separate kill actions, those deaths are sequential. 370.1.a.2 Karthus applies only if the [Deathknell] unit is killed first, because his passive ability is active only while he remains on the board. 365.1 When both units instead have lethal damage during a cleanup, the cleanup kills all lethally damaged units together. 323.4 The other unit's [Deathknell] is added before its source moves to the trash, while Karthus's passive ability is still active. 808.1.d.2 365.1

rulings.question: Does a single Not So Fast counter both Deathknell triggers when Karthus, Eternal is on the board?
rulings.answer: No. If both [Deathknell] triggers are legal targets for Not So Fast , one copy can counter only one of them. When a friendly unit with [Deathknell] dies while Karthus is on the board, his ability causes that [Deathknell] to trigger an additional time. Each trigger is added to the chain as its own independent pending item. 808.1.d.2 Not So Fast targets a single spell or ability, so each copy can counter only one trigger. This applies only when the [Deathknell] ability chooses one of your friendly units or gear. Otherwise, Not So Fast cannot target either trigger.

rulings.question: Can I play a spell at its Action or Reaction timing after Kennen, Storm of Shuriken grants it Flow?
rulings.answer: Yes. A spell that Kennen grants [Flow] keeps its existing timing permissions, whether it has [Action], [Reaction], or neither. Playing the spell for its [Flow] cost does not change the timing at which it can be played or any permission except the zone from which it can be played: your trash. 829.1.b 829.1.b.2

rulings.question: Can Kennen, Storm of Shuriken grant Flow to a spell put into the trash by Minefield's ability triggered by the same conquer?
rulings.answer: No. You must choose a spell already in your trash while Kennen's conquer ability is being finalized on the chain. 403.2 Kennen's ability and Minefield 's ability trigger simultaneously from the same conquer and are added to the chain as pending items. 383.3.d Their order does not change the result because every pending item must be finalized before either ability can resolve. 337.1 337.3 337.4 Minefield therefore cannot put its two cards into your trash until after you have chosen a spell for Kennen's ability, and you cannot later change that choice. 355.15

rulings.question: Can an opponent play a unit in reaction to Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror's trigger to prevent the effect?
rulings.answer: No. Even if an opponent can legally play a unit in reaction, that unit's arrival does not undo Kha'Zix's fulfilled trigger condition. Kha'Zix's ability reads "When I attack or defend, if an enemy unit is alone here, give me +2 this turn and gain 2 XP." The "if" clause immediately follows the initial trigger clause, so it is part of the trigger condition. 383.2.a.1 The condition is evaluated once, when Kha'Zix gains the attacker or defender designation. 383.4.e.2.a 383.4.e.2.b 383.4.f.2.a 383.4.f.2.b If the enemy unit is alone then, the ability is placed on the chain. 383.3 Because the "if" clause is part of the condition rather than the effect, the effect does not check it again during resolution. 383.2.b 407.5 If the enemy unit is not alone then, the ability does not trigger even if another enemy unit is later removed. Playing a legally timed unit places it on the existing chain as a pending item. 330.2 420.1 After it finalizes, the unit resolves immediately and enters the board. 337.2 359.2.c This later entry does not repeat Kha'Zix's earlier trigger-condition check.

rulings.question: Can Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror trigger multiple times in the same turn?
rulings.answer: Yes. In each combat, Kha'Zix can trigger when he first attacks and when he first defends, if an enemy unit is alone at his battlefield at each check. Attack and defend trigger conditions are checked separately when a unit first gains the matching designation during a combat. 383.4.e 383.4.f Each matching check happens only once per combat, rather than once per turn. 383.4.e.2.a 383.4.f.2.a

rulings.question: Can Lacerate target a unit with more than 3 might?
rulings.answer: Yes, Lacerate can target any otherwise legal unit regardless of its might. "Choose a unit" targets a unit and adds no might-based targeting restriction. 355.7 355.9.b The later condition "if it has 3 or less" is checked only when the kill instruction executes during resolution. 359.3.d

rulings.question: Can Last Caress let me play an Ambush unit at a battlefield where I don't control any units?
rulings.answer: Yes, Last Caress lets you play the next unit this turn to a battlefield where you control no units, as long as you could otherwise play it at that time and no restriction or mandatory requirement limits its location. 355.17 355.17.b Last Caress independently makes every battlefield valid for that unit, even when [Ambush]'s own location permission does not apply. 355.2.b 822.3.a This changes only where you may play the unit, not when. Last Caress does not grant [Reaction], and [Ambush] grants [Reaction] only while you are playing the unit to a battlefield where you control units. 822.1.b 813.4

rulings.question: If I play Here to Help from face down, can Last Caress let me play a unit from my hand at a different battlefield?
rulings.answer: No, if Here to Help was played from face down, Last Caress does not let you play the unit from your hand at a different battlefield. Once you choose to play a unit, Here to Help's "to a battlefield you control" instruction is a mandatory requirement on its location. 355.17 Because Here to Help was played from face down, the facedown rules also require that unit to be played at the same battlefield. 811.1.d.5 These requirements do not conflict and must both be followed. 355.17.a Last Caress makes additional battlefields valid locations, but it does not remove either requirement. 355.2.b Any different battlefield fails the facedown requirement, and a battlefield you do not control also fails Here to Help's own requirement. Last Caress's "even from face down" text applies when the next unit itself is played from face down. Here to Help instead instructs you to play the unit from your hand, so that text does not override the requirements imposed by Here to Help and the facedown rules.

rulings.question: How do Reactions that remove units interact with Deceiver's Reflection?
rulings.answer: Deceiver's controller chooses the copy target when the separate reflexive trigger undergoes finalization, after the Reflection token enters: if responses made before the Reflection is played to that battlefield remove every legal copy target from that battlefield, the reflexive trigger leaves the chain without finalizing and the ready Reflection neither becomes a copy nor gains [Temporary]; if, after the Reflection is played to that battlefield and its copy target is chosen, a response removes that target before the reflexive trigger resolves, the Reflection does not become a copy but still gains [Temporary]. The interaction follows this sequence: Deceiver's original trigger finalizes. The copy target is not chosen yet because choices for a reflexive trigger generated by an item are not made while that item is finalized. 355.5.b Once no pending items remain, opponents may respond before the original trigger resolves. 337.4 407.4 The original trigger resolves. It starts playing a ready Reflection token at the battlefield recorded by "there." 359.3.f.3 The token waits as a pending chain item while the original trigger finishes resolving. 354.2 354.3 The reflexive trigger is then added after the token. 389.1 The Reflection enters, then the reflexive trigger reaches finalization. Pending items finalize in the order they were added, so the Reflection finalizes, resolves immediately, and enters before the newer reflexive trigger. 337.1.b 337.2 359.2.c There is no response window between the Reflection entering and the target choice because every pending item must finalize or leave the chain before players can respond. 337.3 337.4 Deceiver's controller must choose another unit at that battlefield as the reflexive trigger's target. 355.10 359.3.f.3.b 403.2 If no other unit there is a legal target, the reflexive trigger is removed without finalizing, 403.4 so the Reflection remains ready but does not become a copy or gain [Temporary]. If a legal target exists, the reflexive trigger finalizes. 407.2 Once no pending items remain, opponents may respond before that trigger resolves. 337.4 407.4 If the chosen unit is no longer legal when the trigger resolves, 359.3.e.2 the copy instruction cannot be followed, so the Reflection does not become a copy. 359.3.e.5 359.3.e.7 The reflexive trigger still resolves and gives the Reflection [Temporary], doing as much of its effect as possible. 055 359.3.e.1 407.5

rulings.question: If my opponent targets my spell with Lilting Lullaby and I counter my own spell in response, can I still play spells?
rulings.answer: Yes. Countering your spell clears it from the chain, so it is an illegal target when Lilting Lullaby resolves. 426.1.a 355.9.a.2 359.3.e.2 Lilting Lullaby still resolves, but its counter instruction is ignored because the target is illegal. 359.3.e.1 359.3.e.5 359.3.e.6 The spell-play restriction is linked to that ignored instruction through "its controller," so the restriction is also ignored. 359.3.e.14 359.3.e.14.a

rulings.question: Does Lotus Trap affect how much damage needs to be assigned in combat?
rulings.answer: Yes, Lotus Trap's doubling applies while combat damage is assigned, so the assigning player uses the doubled amount to determine lethal assignment. A replacement effect that would apply to the resulting damage is considered to apply to the assignment instead. 467.2.c.5 Assigning damage and dealing damage are still distinct steps. 467.2.c.1 A unit must have lethal damage assigned to it in full before any remaining damage may be assigned elsewhere, 467.2.c.3 so the doubling changes how much of the assigning player's damage the unit ties up. For an undamaged 3 unit under Lotus Trap, the minimum is 2 damage: assigning 1 doubles to 2 and is not lethal, while assigning 2 doubles to 4 and is lethal. 467.2.c.4.a When that damage is dealt, it is not doubled again because the replacement was already applied during assignment. 467.2.c.5 If another damage replacement also applies, the unit's controller chooses their order during assignment, which can change both the assigned and dealt amounts. 372 467.2.c.5

rulings.question: Can I use Lux, Crownguard's ability to pay for Hard Bargain?
rulings.answer: No. You can use Lux's ability to add energy to pay the costs of playing a spell, but Hard Bargain 's payment is not a spell play cost. Paying a spell's costs is part of finalizing that spell. 357.1 During that payment, its controller can activate a [Reaction] ability that adds resources. 357.1.a Once the spell finishes finalizing, opponents receive the opportunity to play Reactions such as Hard Bargain. 359.3.a 359.3.c Hard Bargain's instruction, "Counter a spell unless its controller pays ," is executed later, when it resolves. 158.1 The payment is therefore not part of playing the targeted spell. You may still activate Lux's ability, 430.3 but the energy it adds can be spent only to play spells and cannot be spent on Hard Bargain's payment.

rulings.question: Can Iron Revenant banish a unit or gear put into my trash as an additional cost to help pay that play's power cost?
rulings.answer: No, because you pay the played card's energy and power costs before paying its additional cost by discarding a card or killing a unit. You choose whether to pay an optional additional cost before determining the card's total cost. 355.1.a For Atakhan and Commander Ledros , the variable discount from that choice is checked during total-cost determination, before payment begins. 356.4.g During payment, you first pay the combined energy and power costs. 357.1 You then pay non-standard costs, such as discarding a card or killing a unit; "in any order" applies only among those non-standard costs. 357.2 During the energy and power payment step, you may activate Iron Revenant's [Reaction] ability to [Add] power. 357.1.a At that point, the card that will enter your trash for the additional cost isn't there yet. Therefore, Iron Revenant can't banish a unit or gear discarded for Zed, From the Shadows to help pay Zed's power cost. It also can't banish a unit killed for Atakhan or Commander Ledros to help pay the power cost of the card being played.

rulings.question: Can Mordekaiser, Twice Slain save himself by killing another friendly unit that is about to die with him?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Mordekaiser's once-per-turn replacement effect is still available. 371.1 This includes another friendly unit that is about to die from the same combat. Combat damage itself does not kill either unit. The kill action happens during the combat cleanup that follows, which would kill all units with lethal damage simultaneously. 467.2.d 468.1 323.4 370.1.a.2 Here, "simultaneously" describes the kills that cleanup is about to perform; it does not mean those units are already dead. Replacement effects apply before the events they replace, so his effect steps in before the cleanup kills happen. 370.1.c At that point, the other friendly unit is still on the board. It may have lethal damage and be about to die, but you can still kill it to pay the cost of saving him. 740.4.a Paying that cost performs a separate kill action before cleanup performs any simultaneous kills left unchanged. 203.1 373.1.a His own death is replaced, so he is healed, exhausted, and recalled instead. The same timing applies to spells outside combat: Damage followed by a cleanup: If Singularity or Bellows Breath leaves him and another friendly unit with lethal damage, the cleanup waits until the spell finishes resolving. 321 321.1 That cleanup would then kill them simultaneously. 323.4 370.1.a.2 One kill instruction: The Ruination and Cataclysmic Duel each have one kill instruction that can kill multiple units, so any deaths caused by that instruction are simultaneous. 370.1.a.2

rulings.question: Can Mordekaiser, Twice Slain save himself while I control Endless Riches?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Mordekaiser's once-per-turn replacement effect is available and you apply it before Endless Riches whenever both effects apply, then kill another friendly unit for its cost. Mordekaiser is healed, exhausted, and recalled even if Endless Riches banishes that unit's card instead of killing it. If Mordekaiser's card would go to your trash, both effects initially apply to his death, so you choose their order as his controller. 372 If Mordekaiser's effect applies first and you choose another friendly unit, killing that unit is the cost of saving him. 740.4.a If that unit's card would go to your trash, Endless Riches replaces killing it with banishing its card instead. 370.1.a.1 370.2 Replacing its associated game action does not undo the payment. 203.2 If Endless Riches does not apply to the chosen unit, that unit is killed normally to pay the cost. 203.1 Mordekaiser's effect therefore heals, exhausts, and recalls him. If Endless Riches applies to Mordekaiser's original death and you apply it first, it banishes him instead of killing him, leaving no death for his replacement effect to replace. 370.1 370.1.a.1 428.2.a

rulings.question: If an opponent's spell would kill Mordekaiser, Twice Slain, does killing him for his own replacement cost trigger that opponent's Immortal Phoenix in their trash?
rulings.answer: No, because the kill used to pay Mordekaiser's replacement cost is attributed to his ability rather than the opponent's spell and therefore does not trigger Immortal Phoenix . Replacing Mordekaiser's original death means the kill action from the opponent's spell does not occur. 370.1.a.1 Mordekaiser's replacement effect cannot apply again to the kill used to pay that cost. 370.2 You perform that new kill action as the cost, so you are responsible for it. 203.1 412.1 Because Mordekaiser's ability contains the kill instruction, the kill is attributed to that ability and to Mordekaiser, not to the opponent's spell. 412.5 412.5.a 429.5.b 429.5.d An Immortal Phoenix in that opponent's trash triggers only if they are responsible for a kill attributed to a spell they control. 383.2.c.1 412.6

rulings.question: What happens when Mordekaiser, Twice Slain replaces the death Deathgrip would cause?
rulings.answer: When Mordekaiser replaces the death, Deathgrip gives no might and you still draw 1. Under Deathgrip's erratum, its kill instruction is followed by a might instruction conditioned on "If you do" and then a separate draw instruction. Replacing Mordekaiser's death means Deathgrip's kill action does not occur. 370.1.a.1 The conditional might instruction directly references that kill and therefore does not execute, while the draw instruction does not reference it and still executes. 359.3.e.14.b Killing a unit to pay Mordekaiser's replacement cost is a separate kill action attributed to his ability, not the Deathgrip action that was replaced. 203.1 412.5 412.5.a 429.5.b

rulings.question: Can I banish and play Nocturne, Horrifying if Burn or Minefield puts it into my trash?
rulings.answer: Under the interpretation that a player looks at a card only when instructed to do so, no. [Burn] puts cards from the top of your main deck directly into your trash, 441.1 and Minefield gives the same instruction in its printed ability. Neither effect instructs you to look at or reveal Nocturne. Rules citation needed Core Rules 1.5 explains how Nocturne's replacement effect applies when a qualifying look or reveal occurs, but "look" still has no standalone numbered action definition. Unlike reveal, the rules do not expressly state that a player looks at cards only when instructed. This ruling relies on treating "look at" as an instructed event; an official definition is still needed. Nocturne's replacement-effect condition, "As you look at or reveal me from the top of your deck," does not itself instruct you to look at or reveal it. 135.2.b.6 369.1 It can apply only while a qualifying look or reveal event is being processed. 370.1 370.1.c.1 In either case, Nocturne becomes public when it reaches the trash. 108.2.d Under the same interpretation, becoming public does not mean you looked at it from the top of your deck. It also does not mean you revealed it from there because revealing a card is a specific game action performed when instructed. 425.1 425.2.a

rulings.question: Is an equipment's effect text active while Lady of Clockwork makes it a unit gear?
rulings.answer: No. An equipment's effect text is inactive while Lady of Clockwork makes it a unit gear. Effect text is inactive unless its card is attached to another card. 136.2.b For example, a Cloth Armor unit gear's [Shield 2] ability is inactive, so it does not get +2 while defending. 721.2

rulings.question: What happens when Lady of Clockwork makes attached equipment into a unit gear?
rulings.answer: The equipment detaches as it becomes a unit gear and remains at the same location as the card it was attached to. 718.6.a 436.4 After it detaches, its effect text becomes inactive and its printed rules text becomes active again. 436.1.c The card it was attached to stops receiving the equipment's effect text and might bonus. 436.1.d 436.1.e

rulings.question: What happens when I activate Equip on equipment that Lady of Clockwork made into a unit gear?
rulings.answer: You can activate and pay for the [Equip] ability, but the unit gear does not attach when the ability resolves. [Equip] is an activated ability. 818.1 You choose its unit target and pay its cost before resolution. 818.1.b.1 403.2 405.1 Its effect then instructs the source gear to attach to that unit. 818.1.c.2 A unit cannot be attached, so the attach action does nothing. 435.1.h 435.1.h.1

rulings.question: What happens when Shady Spectacles or Mirror Image copies a non-unit gear that Lady of Clockwork made into a unit?
rulings.answer: With either Shady Spectacles or Mirror Image , the resulting copy is a gear, not a unit. While Lady of Clockwork's effect applies, the gear's current unit type satisfies the unit requirement for each effect's choice. 141.1.a.3 355.9.b Lady of Clockwork changes the gear's actual type and might without changing its copyable traits. 479.1.c 479.2 Copy effects use the gear's printed traits, the traits it had when created as a token, or traits supplied by an existing copy effect, so they do not include Lady of Clockwork's changes. 479.1.b 479.1.b.1

rulings.question: What happens when Lady of Clockwork makes Deploy gear into a unit at an uncontested battlefield its controller does not control?
rulings.answer: The gear applies contested status to that battlefield, and the next cleanup stages combat if an opposing unit is there or a non-combat showdown otherwise. That combat or showdown opens after the chain is empty. When Lady of Clockwork's ability resolves, the [Deploy] gear becomes a unit at its existing location. A unit that becomes present at a battlefield its controller does not control applies contested status there. 190.3.a The resulting cleanup stages a showdown. 323.7 If opposing units are present, it also stages combat. 323.8 A staged showdown or combat waits until no items remain on the chain before opening. 323.11 323.12 331.2

rulings.question: When does Lady of Clockwork's unit gear become a non-unit gear again?
rulings.answer: Lady of Clockwork's previous effect stops granting the old gear its unit type and might as soon as her controller chooses another gear during finalization, before the new ability resolves. If this leaves it as an unattached non-unit gear at a battlefield and it does not have [Deploy], the cleanup after finalization recalls it before players can respond. Lady of Clockwork's gear choice is made during finalization. 403.2 Lady of Clockwork's stated duration therefore ends when the new gear is chosen, not when the ability resolves. Finalizing the ability makes a cleanup outstanding. 319.4 That cleanup must finish before play proceeds. 334.2.a The new ability cannot resolve during it. 320 Priority is not passed or awarded during it. 320.1 During that cleanup, an unattached non-unit gear at a battlefield is recalled unless it has [Deploy]. 459.1

rulings.question: What happens to attached equipment when Lady of Clockwork's unit gear stops being a unit?
rulings.answer: The equipment stays attached when Lady of Clockwork's unit gear stops being a unit. The equipment is the attached card, while the unit gear is the top-most card. 717 Only the attached card must remain a non-unit. 718.6 It remains attached until something detaches it. 718.1 If the gear is recalled after losing its unit type, the attached equipment changes locations with it. 719.3.a Example Lady of Clockwork makes Helm of Suppression a unit gear, then Svellsongur attaches to it. Svellsongur copies Helm of Suppression's printed rules text into its effect text for as long as it remains attached. 479.1.b.1 When Lady of Clockwork chooses another gear, Helm of Suppression stops being a unit but Svellsongur remains attached. The copied effect text remains appended to Helm of Suppression's rules text, so Helm of Suppression is a non-unit gear with two instances of its printed rules text. 719.1

rulings.question: How does Promising Future resolve?
rulings.answer: First, every player chooses and banishes a card, starting with the turn player. 303.2.a Then, starting with the next player, every player starts playing their chosen card by putting it on the chain. The chosen cards do not proceed to finalization while Promising Future is still resolving. 354.2 354.3 Steps Starting with the turn player and proceeding in turn order, each player looks at their top 5 cards, banishes one, then recycles the rest. 303.2.a The cards already banished are public information, so each later player knows what the players before them chose. 108.6.e Starting with the next player and proceeding in turn order, each player puts their banished card on the chain as a pending item. Each card waits for finalization while Promising Future continues resolving. Promising Future finishes resolving. This completes the act of playing Promising Future, so applicable abilities on cards such as Ravenbloom Student trigger and are put on the chain after the chosen cards. 383.3 420.4.a The chosen cards then proceed to finalization in the order they were put on the chain: the next player's card first, followed by each other player in turn order. 337.1.b Their base energy costs are set to zero, but their power costs, applicable additional costs, and later cost increases still apply. 356.1.b.2 356.1.b.3 If a player cannot pay every required cost, that card's play process is undone and it returns to banishment. 358.2 358.5 A unit or gear that finalizes resolves immediately and enters the board. 337.2 359.2.c 359.2.d Its own play effect is put on the chain after it enters. 383.4.a.2 Any other ability whose trigger condition was fulfilled by that entry is likewise put on the chain after the inciting event. 383.2.c 383.3 Because those abilities were added after the chosen cards, every chosen card finalizes or leaves the chain before those abilities finalize. 337.1 337.1.b If any finalized spells or abilities remain, the controller of the newest one receives priority. 337.4 Players may then play Reactions. 338.1.a 338.1.a.2 In that case, after all players pass priority without adding another item, finalized spells and abilities resolve from newest to oldest. 339.1 340.1 Example In a two-player game, the turn player chooses and banishes first, so their opponent knows that choice before making their own. The opponent then puts their card on the chain first, followed by the turn player. If both cards are permanents and both finalize, the opponent's permanent enters first. If both are spells, the turn player's spell is newer and resolves first, after any items played or triggered above it.

rulings.question: Can a counterspell chosen with Promising Future counter another chosen card?
rulings.answer: Yes, if another chosen card is an eligible spell that finalizes before the counterspell and is a legal target when the counterspell is finalized. Promising Future puts every chosen card on the chain as a pending item before any of them proceed to finalization. 354.2 354.3 Players choose only which card to banish during Promising Future's first pass. The counterspell's target is chosen later, during that counterspell's finalization. 355.5 A counterspell cannot finalize without a valid target. 355.8 If no valid target exists, its play process is undone and it returns to banishment. 358.5 Example In a two-player game, suppose the turn player banishes a counterspell. The opponent's card is put on the chain first, followed by the turn player's counterspell, so the opponent's card undergoes finalization first. 337.1.b If the opponent chose a spell that the counterspell can target, the turn player can choose that spell while finalizing the counterspell. The counterspell is newer and therefore resolves first, allowing it to counter the opponent's spell before that spell resolves. 340.1 426.1.a A counterspell put on the chain before another chosen card must finalize or leave the chain while that later card is still pending. 337.1 337.1.b Only a finalized spell or ability on the chain can be a legal target, so the counterspell cannot target that later card. 355.9.a

rulings.question: Can Salvage or Brittle Steel target Dazzling Aurora if both are chosen with Promising Future?
rulings.answer: In a two-player game, Salvage or Brittle Steel can target Dazzling Aurora only if Promising Future's controller chose the spell and their opponent chose Aurora. If Promising Future's controller chose Aurora and their opponent chose the spell, that spell cannot target Aurora. Promising Future puts the next player's chosen card on the chain first, so the opponent's card finalizes first. 337.1.b A gear that finalizes resolves immediately and enters the board. 337.2 359.2.d A spell chooses its targets during its own finalization, and a gear target must be on the board unless another zone is specified. 355.5 355.9.a 355.9.a.1 If the opponent chose Aurora, it enters the board before Promising Future's controller's spell chooses its target. If the opponent chose the spell, it must choose its target while Aurora is still pending on the chain, so Aurora is not a legal target. Both spells may choose another legal gear instead. Salvage may also choose no gear, while Brittle Steel's play is undone if no legal gear is available. 355.8 358.5

rulings.question: Does Brynhir Thundersong stop an opponent's card chosen with Promising Future from being played?
rulings.answer: Only if Brynhir Thundersong 's play effect has already resolved when Promising Future instructs that opponent to play their chosen card. Brynhir's restriction supersedes Promising Future's permission to play the card. 054.1 That play instruction is negated, so the chosen card remains banished. 359.3.e.6 Brynhir prevents an opponent from performing the play game action, which puts the card on the chain and queues it for finalization. 420.1 420.5 If Brynhir herself is chosen with Promising Future, she does not stop any other chosen card. Promising Future puts every chosen card on the chain as a pending item before any of them proceed to finalization. 354.2 354.3 Brynhir's play effect is added only after she finalizes and enters the board. 383.4.a.2 By then, every chosen card has already been added to the chain and queued for finalization, so Brynhir's restriction cannot prevent those play game actions. 420.5

rulings.question: When I choose Akshan, Mischievous with Promising Future, do I have to pay his additional cost before knowing whether I can take Dazzling Aurora?
rulings.answer: No. Every player chooses and banishes a card before Promising Future instructs anyone to play one. Because cards in banishment are public information, 108.6.e you, as Akshan, Mischievous 's controller, know whether your opponent chose Dazzling Aurora before deciding whether to pay Akshan's additional cost. You can then choose Dazzling Aurora for Akshan's play effect. Promising Future puts every chosen card on the chain as a pending item before any of them proceed to finalization. 354.2 354.3 You decide whether to pay Akshan's optional additional cost while Akshan is being finalized, not when he is banished or first put on the chain. 355.1.a His play effect is a separate pending ability put on the chain after Akshan finalizes and enters the board. 383.4.a.2 You choose the enemy gear while that triggered ability is being finalized. 403.2 It isn't chosen while Akshan is being finalized. 355.5.b This differs from a spell that chooses a gear itself, because that choice is made while the spell is finalized. 355.5 Akshan's play effect is instead a separate, newer pending item, so every chosen card finalizes or leaves the chain before that ability finalizes. 337.1 337.1.b 383.4.a.2 Dazzling Aurora Is Banished First The turn player banishes Dazzling Aurora. Because banished cards are public, you see that choice before selecting Akshan from your own top 5 cards. Starting with the next player, Akshan is put on the chain first and Dazzling Aurora second. Akshan finalizes first. You already know Dazzling Aurora was selected and may choose to pay Akshan's additional cost, even though Aurora is still pending. 355.1.a Akshan enters the board, and his play effect is put on the chain after Dazzling Aurora. 383.4.a.2 Dazzling Aurora is the older pending item, so it finalizes next and enters the board before Akshan's play effect is finalized. 337.1.b 337.2 359.2.d Akshan's play effect then finalizes. Dazzling Aurora is now an enemy gear on the board, and you can choose it for that ability. 403.2 Akshan, Mischievous Is Banished First If Akshan is banished first, your opponent sees Akshan before choosing Dazzling Aurora. Dazzling Aurora is then put on the chain first and enters before Akshan is finalized. You therefore see Dazzling Aurora on the board when deciding whether to pay the additional cost.

rulings.question: Can Disarming Rake or Tomb-Raider Barbara kill Dazzling Aurora if chosen with Promising Future?
rulings.answer: Disarming Rake can kill Dazzling Aurora regardless of order, and Tomb-Raider Barbara can also kill Aurora regardless of order if Barbara's controller controls 7 or more runes when she is played and Aurora is an enemy gear that isn't [Empowered] when the play effect resolves. Promising Future puts every chosen card on the chain as a pending item before any of them proceed to finalization. 354.2 354.3 Both units' "When you play me" abilities are play effects. 383.4.a 383.4.a.1 Barbara's rune requirement is part of her trigger condition, so her play effect triggers only if that requirement is met when she is played. 383.2.a.1 Each play effect that triggers is put on the chain as a separate pending item only after its unit finalizes and enters the board. 383.4.a.2 If Dazzling Aurora finalizes first, it is already on the board when the unit's play effect is finalized. If either unit finalizes first, its play effect is put on the chain after Dazzling Aurora, so the older Aurora finalizes and enters before the ability is finalized. 337.1.b 337.2 359.2.d In either order, Aurora is on the board by the time the play effect chooses a gear. 403.2

rulings.question: Can Ravenbloom Prefect banish Dazzling Aurora if both are chosen with Promising Future?
rulings.answer: Only if Dazzling Aurora is played by an opponent of Ravenbloom Prefect 's controller and Ravenbloom Prefect finalizes before Aurora. Promising Future puts every chosen card on the chain as a pending item before any of them proceed to finalization. 354.2 354.3 Ravenbloom Prefect's ability triggers when an opponent plays a gear; it is not Prefect's own play effect. 383.4.a.4 Prefect must therefore be on the board when Dazzling Aurora finishes being played for that trigger condition to be fulfilled. 384.2 383.2.c 420.4.a If Ravenbloom Prefect finalizes first, it enters before Dazzling Aurora finalizes. When the opposing player finishes playing Aurora, Prefect's ability triggers and is put on the chain. 383.3 Prefect's controller may then banish Prefect to finalize that ability and banish Dazzling Aurora when the ability resolves. 383.3.a 383.3.b 383.3.b.1 If Dazzling Aurora finalizes first, Ravenbloom Prefect is still a pending card on the chain when Aurora enters. The ability does not trigger later when Prefect enters.

rulings.question: When do I choose whether to make Rebuttal's optional payment?
rulings.answer: You choose the affected spell during Rebuttal's finalization, before opponents can react. 355.5 359.3.c You do not decide whether to pay until Rebuttal resolves. The optional payment is not a cost paid to play Rebuttal; it is a game action Rebuttal instructs you to perform during resolution. 135.2.b.3 205 Opponents therefore know which spell you chose, but not whether you will pay to gain control of it or decline and have Rebuttal attempt to counter it.

rulings.question: What choices can I remake when Rebuttal takes control of a spell?
rulings.answer: You may decline to make new choices and leave every existing choice unchanged, or remake every eligible choice the spell made. 753 The eligible categories are play locations, modes, move destinations, and targets, all of which are choices normally made during finalization. 752 752.1 Choices made "as you play this" and choices about optional additional costs cannot be remade. 752.2 If you make new choices, every resulting choice must be legal. 753.1 You cannot choose to make new choices unless a complete legal set is available. 753.2 You may select the same option again, but it still counts as remaking that choice. 753 If the spell targets a game object after you remake its choices, that object's applicable targeting effects trigger, even if the spell targeted it before. 754 If you decline, the existing choices remain unchanged even if a target has become illegal. 355.15 The spell still resolves, but an illegal target is unaffected. 359.3.e.1 359.3.e.5

rulings.question: Can Rebuttal redirect a spell played from face down to another location?
rulings.answer: No. Restrictions already applied to a spell, including the targeting restriction imposed by [Hidden], also apply to its new choices. 753.3 Rebuttal allows you to remake a finalized spell's targets, 752.1 but every new target must still be legal. 753.1 When a spell is played from face down, its targets must be chosen from among the options at the battlefield where it was hidden unless the spell's own targeting restriction makes that impossible. 811.1.d.2 Changing the spell's controller does not change where it was played from, so this restriction continues to apply. Example An opponent plays Hidden Blade from face down and chooses a unit at that battlefield. If you gain control of Hidden Blade with Rebuttal, you may choose another legal unit at the same battlefield. You cannot choose a unit at another battlefield, and you cannot choose a unit at base because Hidden Blade itself requires a unit "at a battlefield."

rulings.question: Whose "when you play a spell" abilities trigger for a spell Rebuttal takes control of?
rulings.answer: Under the August 2026 Vendetta FAQ , if the spell resolves after Rebuttal takes control of it, the spell's new controller's applicable "when you play a spell" abilities trigger; the original player's abilities do not. These abilities trigger once the spell has finished resolving. 420.4.a Rebuttal has made the player who gained control of the spell its controller by then. Rules citation needed Core Rules 1.5 says an ability that triggers when "you" do something checks for a game action for which that player is responsible. 412.4 It does not say that gaining control of a finalized spell transfers responsibility for the spell's earlier play game action. The new-controller outcome above therefore still relies on the official FAQ ruling. Example Suppose you and your opponent each control Ravenbloom Student , and you use Rebuttal to gain control of your opponent's Gust . Your Ravenbloom Student triggers when Rebuttal resolves under your control. If Gust then resolves under your control, your Ravenbloom Student triggers again, while your opponent's Ravenbloom Student does not trigger for Gust.

rulings.question: When do I spend Riven, Broken Blade's buff for her second and third modes?
rulings.answer: Riven's buff costs appear later in her triggered effect, so you spend them during resolution, not during finalization. The "Spend my buff to..." wording makes spending the buff a cost within instructions for the linked [Stun] or ready effect. 740.4.a Riven's effect starts with "choose one," so those costs appear later in the triggered effect. Costs that appear later in a triggered effect are paid during resolution. 204.3.a Rules citation needed Core Rules 1.5 is internally inconsistent here. One rule broadly says that a triggered ability's cost within instructions becomes its base cost. 404.1.b.1 That wording does not distinguish later modal costs such as Riven's and conflicts with the position-based rule above. This ruling follows the position-based rule; official clarification is still needed. Choose the mode and any target it requires during finalization. 355.10 403.2 If Riven has no buff when resolution reaches the chosen instruction, you cannot spend one. 702.2.b.1 Because the cost cannot be paid, the linked [Stun] or ready effect does not occur. 203.3

rulings.question: Can I choose Riven, Broken Blade's "Buff me" mode if she already has a buff?
rulings.answer: Yes, as long as that mode has not already been chosen this turn. A unit that already has a buff can still be chosen for an effect that would buff it. 427.1.c You choose Riven's mode during finalization. 403.2 When the ability resolves, Riven receives no additional buff, so the chosen mode has no effect. 427.1.b.1

rulings.question: Do Zhonya's Hourglass and Guardian Angel trigger Riven, Broken Blade when they save her?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Riven is ready when either replacement effect applies; no, if she is already exhausted. Both Zhonya's Hourglass and Guardian Angel replace Riven's death with instructions that heal, exhaust, and recall her. 369.1 370.1.b If Riven is ready, exhausting her changes her state to exhausted and fulfills her trigger condition. 415.1 370.1.a 383.2.c If she is already exhausted, she cannot be exhausted again and the instruction does nothing additional, so her condition is not fulfilled and her ability does not trigger. 415.1.b 415.1.c 383.3

rulings.question: Can I channel with Ruined Monastery if I have no cards in hand?
rulings.answer: Yes, you still channel 1 rune exhausted with Ruined Monastery if you have no cards in hand. Its "discard 1 and channel 1 rune exhausted" wording does not use the "[do X] to [do Y]" form that creates a cost within instructions, so discarding is part of the effect rather than a cost. 740.4.a The impossible discard instruction is therefore negated, and the channel instruction still happens. 055 423.4 If it instead said "discard 1 to channel 1 rune exhausted," discarding would be a cost. With an empty hand, that cost would be impossible to pay, so you would not channel. 203.3

rulings.question: Does Ruined Rex's Deathknell deal damage before or after units are healed at the end of combat?
rulings.answer: Ruined Rex's [Deathknell] deals damage after the surviving units are healed. The combat cleanup adds the ability as a pending item. 808.1.d.2 That cleanup heals all surviving units before the pending ability can begin finalization. 468.1.a.1 320 334.2 If a legal enemy unit is available, the trigger's controller must choose one as its target during finalization. 355.10 403.2 403.4.b Once no pending items remain, the controller of the next item receives priority before the trigger resolves. 337.4 It deals 4 damage to the chosen enemy unit.

rulings.question: Can Ruined Rex's Deathknell target the Mech tokens created by Ferrous Forerunner's Deathknell, if both die at the same time?
rulings.answer: No. The trigger's controller chooses its target before Ferrous Forerunner creates its Mech tokens. When both units die in the same cleanup, their [Deathknell] abilities become pending items. 808.1.d.2 Each pending item finalizes or leaves the chain before priority is awarded. 337.1 337.3 337.4 The trigger's controller chooses its target during ability finalization. 355.10 403.2 Ferrous Forerunner creates its Mechs only when its ability later resolves. 340.1 Regardless of finalization order, those Mechs do not exist when the trigger's controller chooses its target. That choice cannot change when Ferrous Forerunner's ability later resolves. 355.15

rulings.question: When is my "next Ending Phase" for Runeblade Anvil?
rulings.answer: For Runeblade Anvil, your "next Ending Phase" is whichever of your Ending Phases begins first after its triggered ability resolves. The ability creates the play permission when it executes. 407.5 That permission remains active only for the time stated by the effect. 391.4 392 Earlier in your turn: If the ability resolves before that turn's Ending Phase begins, that same Ending Phase is next. 316.9.b The permission ends when the game enters that phase. During your Ending Phase or another player's turn: If the ability resolves during your Ending Phase, that phase has already begun. If it resolves during another player's turn, that turn's Ending Phase isn't yours. In either case, your next Ending Phase begins on your following turn. 115.1.c 317.3 The permission ends when that phase begins.

rulings.question: If Sacrifice is countered, is the killed unit returned?
rulings.answer: No. Killing a friendly [Mighty] unit is an additional cost paid while playing Sacrifice. 356.7 357.2 Countering the spell later does not refund that cost, so the killed unit is not returned. 426.1.c 426.1.c.1

rulings.question: Can Mordekaiser, Twice Slain survive being chosen for Sacrifice's additional cost?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Mordekaiser, Twice Slain is [Mighty], his once-per-turn replacement effect is available, and you kill another friendly unit for its cost. 371.1 Mordekaiser is healed, exhausted, and recalled, while Sacrifice's additional cost remains paid. Sacrifice's additional cost attempts to kill Mordekaiser while the spell is being finalized. 356.7 357.2 Mordekaiser's effect replaces his death, so Sacrifice's kill action does not occur. 370.1.a.1 The kill action being replaced does not undo its payment as a cost, so Sacrifice can finish finalizing. 357.2.a Killing the other friendly unit pays the cost of Mordekaiser's replacement effect, which then heals, exhausts, and recalls him. 203.1 740.4.a

rulings.question: Can my opponent play a reaction after I choose the Mighty unit for Sacrifice's additional cost but before I kill it?
rulings.answer: No. Your opponent has no normal reaction window after you choose the [Mighty] unit but before you kill it. Costs are paid during step 4 of finalization, and finalization does not pass priority. 357.2 337.1.a During that step, as Sacrifice's controller, you may activate an eligible [Add] ability with [Reaction] when resources are required, even without priority. 357.1.a 430.3 This limited exception does not create a normal reaction window or permit your opponent to play a spell like Stupefy between choosing and killing the unit. 430.2.a

rulings.question: Does the Deathknell of the unit killed as the cost resolve before Sacrifice draws and channels?
rulings.answer: Yes. The unit is killed while Sacrifice's additional cost is being paid. 356.7 357.2 Its [Deathknell] is therefore added above Sacrifice as a pending ability. 808.1.d.2 The [Deathknell] resolves before Sacrifice draws and channels. 337.1.b 340.1 Steps Sacrifice moves to the chain as a pending spell. 354.2 Its controller then pays the additional cost by killing a friendly [Mighty] unit. That unit's [Deathknell] is added above Sacrifice as a pending ability before the unit moves to the trash. 808.1.d.2 Sacrifice finishes finalizing. 359.3.a The pending [Deathknell] then finalizes. 337.1 359.3.b 407.2 The [Deathknell] resolves before Sacrifice. Sacrifice then resolves, drawing 2 and channeling 1 rune exhausted. 359.3.d

rulings.question: Can Seraphine, Not Alone survive combat damage that becomes lethal when other exhausted units die in the same combat?
rulings.answer: Yes, if Seraphine does not have lethal damage when the combat cleanup checks her while those other exhausted units are still on the board. The cleanup checks all units for lethal damage only once, so damage that becomes lethal after those units leave does not kill Seraphine during that cleanup. 323.4 Three-Recruit Sequence Suppose Seraphine has 3 damage marked and gets +3 from three other exhausted Recruit tokens, each with 1 and 1 damage marked. She therefore has 4 . Lethal-damage check: Seraphine's 3 marked damage is less than her current 4 , while each Recruit's 1 marked damage equals its 1 . 142.4.b Only the Recruits have lethal damage during the check, so the cleanup kills them and not Seraphine. 323.4 Once the Recruits leave the board, they are no longer exhausted units for Seraphine's ability to count. 415.2 Her continuously evaluated might bonus therefore disappears, returning her to 1 . 478.1 479.4.a Her 3 marked damage is now lethal. 142.4.b That cleanup does not check her again. Combat healing: The combat special cleanup next heals all units, clearing Seraphine's marked damage. 468.1.a.1 The Recruits' departure causes another cleanup after the combat cleanup finishes. 319.6 322 Seraphine has no marked damage when that cleanup checks for lethal damage, so she survives. 323.4

rulings.question: Does Shadow Assassin count itself when I play it from my trash?
rulings.answer: No. When played from your trash, Shadow Assassin moves from your trash to the chain, then leaves the chain as it enters the board. 354 359.2 359.2.c By the time its ready condition applies, that copy is no longer in your trash, so it enters ready only if a different card named Shadow Assassin remains in your trash.

rulings.question: When I play Shadowblade Lurker from my trash, does it count itself for its cost reduction?
rulings.answer: No. The first step of playing Shadowblade Lurker moves it from your trash to the chain, so that copy is no longer in your trash. 354 The number of matching cards is checked afterward when its discount is applied, so only other cards named Shadowblade Lurker in your trash at that time count toward the reduction. 356.4.g

rulings.question: Does Shady Spectacles copy Temporary from the chosen unit?
rulings.answer: Shady Spectacles copies [Temporary] when the keyword comes from the chosen unit's card, its token definition, or a copy effect, but not when another effect granted it. For example, copying Keeper of Masks gives the equipped unit [Temporary] because the keyword is printed on Keeper of Masks. If a unit has [Temporary] only because it received the keyword from Shadow's Call , Deceiver , or Mirror Image , Shady Spectacles does not copy it. In rules terms, copy effects use copyable traits: a card's printed or already-copied traits, or the traits a token had when it was created. 479.1.b 479.1.b.1 A separate keyword grant changes what the unit currently has without changing those copyable traits. 479.1.c 479.3.a

rulings.question: Can Guardian Angel, Zhonya's Hourglass, or Tactical Retreat save a unit from Smite?
rulings.answer: Yes, if the unit's controller applies the protective death replacement before Smite's replacement; if they apply Smite's first, the unit is banished. All of these effects replace the same death event, so the affected unit's controller chooses their order. 372 Smite's "if it would die this turn, banish it instead" is a replacement effect. 369.1 Guardian Angel , Zhonya's Hourglass , and Tactical Retreat also replace a unit's death. If the controller applies one of those protective effects first, the kill action does not occur and the unit is healed, exhausted, and recalled. 370.1.a.1 For the first two effects, the gear also dies in the unit's place. None of those replacement actions is another death event for the affected unit, so Smite has no qualifying event left to replace. 370.1.b If Smite's effect is applied first, it replaces the unit's death with banishment. Banishment is not a kill, 428.2.a so none of the protective effects applies afterward.

rulings.question: Does Sunken Temple trigger if I conquer with a unit that is only Mighty due to Assault?
rulings.answer: Yes, if [Assault] raises at least one of your conquering units to 5 or more. 708 710 The conquer occurs before combat ends. 468.5.d 468.7 The unit's attacker designation is removed only afterward, so its [Assault] bonus still applies when Sunken Temple checks whether it is [Mighty]. 468.7.a 807.1.c 807.1.d.1

rulings.question: How does Switcheroo work?
rulings.answer: Switcheroo reverses the units' current might when it resolves, but it does not exchange their base might or set either unit's might to a new value. The Swap action determines the difference between the two current values, then creates a might increase for the lower value and an equal might decrease for the higher value. 434.1 434.1.a 434.1.b Each increase or decrease lasts for Switcheroo's stated duration, this turn. 434.1.a If the units have equal might when Switcheroo resolves, the Swap has no effect. 434.1.c

rulings.question: Are existing equipment bonuses or passive effects counted again after Switcheroo resolves?
rulings.answer: No, each existing modifier is counted once as part of the unit's current might, and it continues applying normally after Switcheroo resolves. 478.2 479.4.a 479.4.d Switcheroo calculates one difference from the complete current values and creates separate increase and decrease effects; it does not remove, reapply, or replace the existing modifiers. 434.1.a 434.1.b For example, if a unit has a base might of 2 and an active +3 bonus, its current might is 5 for the Swap calculation. After the Swap, the +3 remains one part of that unit's might rather than being added a second time.

rulings.question: What happens when equipment detaches or passives stop applying after Switcheroo?
rulings.answer: Only the modifier that stops applying changes the unit's might. 478.4 479.4.a Switcheroo's increase or decrease keeps its originally calculated amount until end of turn. The Swap creates effects with fixed amounts when it resolves, so later changes do not cause it to recalculate the difference. 434.1.a 434.1.b Example Wuju Bladesman - Starter grants a friendly unit +2 while it defends alone. Suppose your Pakaa Cub has 3 before that bonus and defends alone, while an opposing Determined Sentry attacks with 1 . The bonus from Wuju Bladesman raises Pakaa Cub to 5 . Your opponent plays Switcheroo targeting both units. Switcheroo gives Pakaa Cub -4 and Determined Sentry +4 , leaving them at 1 and 5 , respectively. If Pakaa Cub stops defending alone, it loses that +2 bonus but keeps Switcheroo's -4 decrease, leaving it at -1 .

rulings.question: Can Switcheroo result in negative might?
rulings.answer: Yes, a unit can have negative might if a bonus included in Switcheroo's calculation stops applying while Switcheroo's decrease remains. 434.1.a 434.1.b 478.4 Spells, abilities, and combat-damage assignment treat negative might as 0 . 143.2.c Might increases and decreases instead use the actual negative value. 143.2.c.1 The unit does not die merely for having 0 or negative might. At cleanup, it is killed only if it has a non-zero amount of marked damage equal to or greater than its might. 142.4.b 323.4 Example A Scuttle Crab at -2 is targeted with Punch First , which reads "Give a unit +5 this turn." Scuttle Crab ends up with 3 because the +5 increase uses -2 , not 0 .

rulings.question: When I play Temporal Breach from face down, can it banish a unit at a different battlefield?
rulings.answer: No. "Banish a unit" targets the mentioned unit, 355.10 and when you play Temporal Breach from face down, you must choose its targets from the battlefield where it was hidden. 811.1.d.2 A unit at another battlefield or a base is therefore not a legal target. If you play Temporal Breach normally, the [Hidden] restriction does not apply. You may target an otherwise legal unit at any battlefield or base. 355.9.a 811.3

rulings.question: Does a unit keep temporary modifications or statuses when Temporal Breach banishes it and its owner plays it again?
rulings.answer: No. Moving from the board to banishment makes the unit a new game object and clears its temporary modifications and statuses. 056.1 124 124.1 For example, Stupefy 's might reduction no longer applies, and the unit is no longer [Empowered]. 124.2

rulings.question: What happens to equipment attached to a unit banished by Temporal Breach?
rulings.answer: The equipment detaches at the unit's previous location and does not reattach when the unit is played again. Moving the unit from the board to banishment detaches its attached cards at that last location. 719.5 436.4.b The unit entering the board is a new game object, and Temporal Breach does not instruct the equipment to attach again. 124 Detached equipment at a battlefield is recalled to its controller's base during the next cleanup. 436.4.a Detached equipment at a base its controller does not control is recalled to its controller's base during cleanup. 323.6 Equipment already at its controller's base remains there. 323.6

rulings.question: Can Temporal Breach cause a unit's attack or defend ability to trigger again during the same combat?
rulings.answer: Yes, if the unit enters the battlefield where combat is occurring and its attack or defend condition is otherwise fulfilled. 383.4.e.2.b 383.4.f.2.b The unit entering the battlefield is a new game object, so its attack or defend condition has not been checked during that combat. 124 383.4.e.2.a 383.4.f.2.a During the cleanup after it re-enters, it gains the same attacker or defender designation as its controller. 466.2.c.3.a Gaining that designation checks the corresponding attack or defend trigger. 383.4.e 383.4.f Example Ahri, Inquisitive 's "When I attack or defend" ability triggers when she first gains the defender designation. If Temporal Breach then banishes her and her owner plays her again at that battlefield, the new Ahri object gains the designation during cleanup and can trigger the ability again.

rulings.question: Does Ravenbloom Conservatory trigger again if Temporal Breach banishes my only defending unit and I play it again?
rulings.answer: No. "You" in Ravenbloom Conservatory 's ability means its controller, so if you control Ravenbloom Conservatory, it checks its "When you defend here" condition when you gain the defender designation as combat opens. 190.6.d 383.4.f 466.2.c.3 That defend condition is checked only once per combat. 383.4.f.2.a The unit becomes a new game object, but Ravenbloom Conservatory does not. 124 As the defending player, you keep the defender designation until combat ends, so the unit's return does not cause you to gain it again. 468.7.a

rulings.question: What happens if Temporal Breach banishes a token unit?
rulings.answer: The token ceases to exist in banishment, so its owner cannot play it again. Tokens can exist only on the board or the chain and cease to exist immediately after entering another non-board zone. 056.1 186 186.1

rulings.question: Can I pay optional additional costs, like Accelerate, when playing a unit banished by Temporal Breach?
rulings.answer: Yes. Playing the unit "ignoring its cost" sets only its base energy and power costs to zero. 356.1.b.1 Additional costs apply afterward and can raise the total cost above zero. 356.1.b.3 As the unit's owner, you may therefore choose and pay an optional additional cost during finalization. 355.1.a 356.2.b.1 For example, [Accelerate] remains available because it is an optional additional cost paid while playing the unit. 805.2

rulings.question: What happens if a unit's owner can't pay a mandatory additional cost when Temporal Breach instructs them to play it?
rulings.answer: The attempted play is cancelled, and the unit returns to its owner's banishment. Temporal Breach sets only the unit's base energy and power costs to zero, so mandatory additional costs must still be paid. 356.1.b.1 356.2.a.1 If the owner cannot pay one, the play fails its cost check. 358.2 The play is then cancelled and its actions are undone, returning the unit from the chain to its owner's banishment without undoing Temporal Breach's earlier, completed instruction. 354 358.5 Example If Temporal Breach banishes Cruel Patron and its owner has no other friendly unit, they can't pay Cruel Patron's mandatory additional cost to kill a friendly unit. Cruel Patron cannot finish finalizing and returns to its owner's banishment.

rulings.question: If the unit banished by Temporal Breach has Hidden, can its owner hide it instead of playing it?
rulings.answer: No. Hide is a separate action, not a way to play a card. 811.1.c.1 Playing puts the unit on the chain for finalization, while hiding would put it facedown at a battlefield. 420.1 422.1 The unit is also in banishment, but [Hidden] permits hiding only from hand or the champion zone. 811.1.b

rulings.question: Can Temporal Breach make me conquer the same battlefield again on my opponent's turn?
rulings.answer: No. You retain control of the battlefield while Temporal Breach banishes your only unit there and that unit is played again, so you do not conquer it again. 471.1 The unit remains pending on the chain through cleanup, so you do not lose and regain control of the battlefield. 323.5 330 334.2 Cleanup can remove your control of an empty battlefield only when no chain exists. 190.4.c 309.1 Steps Banishment leaves you with no units at the battlefield and incurs a cleanup, but that cleanup waits for Temporal Breach to finish resolving. 319.6 321.1 The unit's owner begins playing it by moving it to the chain, where it remains pending while Temporal Breach finishes resolving. 354 354.2 354.3 The pending unit remains on the chain throughout the cleanup, so you retain control. The unit then finalizes and enters the same battlefield under its owner's control. 191.2 191.4 334.2 337.1 359.2.c

rulings.question: Can Rockfall Path or Brynhir Thundersong stop the unit from being played after Temporal Breach banishes it?
rulings.answer: Both effects can stop the unit from being played and leave it in its owner's banishment, but Rockfall Path does not stop the play process from starting, while a resolved Brynhir Thundersong effect that applies to the unit's owner does. With Rockfall Path, the owner begins playing the unit, moving it from banishment to the chain as a pending card. 354 354.2 420.3.b Its finalization waits until Temporal Breach finishes resolving. 354.3 Temporal Breach requires the unit to be played to its previous location, but Rockfall Path forbids units from being played there, so the unit fails its legality check. 355.17 355.17.b 358.1 That play is cancelled and undone, returning the unit to its owner's banishment. 358.5 With Brynhir Thundersong, the owner cannot begin the play game action, so the unit never leaves banishment. 054.1 420.3.c 420.5 The impossible play instruction is negated, and Temporal Breach continues resolving after doing as much as possible. 055 358.3.a 359.3.e.6

rulings.question: If I own and control a unit at a battlefield I control, can Thrill of the Hunt make me conquer that battlefield again on my opponent's turn?
rulings.answer: No. Thrill of the Hunt instructs the banished unit's owner to play it to any battlefield. Because you own the unit in this scenario, you choose that battlefield. If you choose the original battlefield, the unit remains on the chain throughout cleanup while being played again, so you keep control until it returns. 330 354.4 309.1 323.5 Because you do not gain control again, you do not conquer the battlefield again. 471.1 The following sequence applies when you choose the original battlefield. Unit becomes pending: Thrill of the Hunt banishes the unit and instructs you, as its owner, to play it before the resulting cleanup runs. 319.6 321.1 The unit moves to the chain as a pending item while Thrill of the Hunt finishes resolving. 354.2 354.3 Cleanup: The pending unit keeps the chain in progress while cleanup runs, so cleanup does not remove your battlefield control. Unit enters: After cleanup, the unit finalizes and enters the same battlefield. 334.2 337.1 359.2.c

rulings.question: Can Transpositionist still play a unit when an Empowered Gangplank, Naval replaces the return?
rulings.answer: When an [Empowered] Gangplank, Naval replaces Transpositionist's return, you may still play a unit that has less might than Gangplank's current might after the +3 increase applies, provided that unit is in your hand or chosen champion zone or a separate effect permits you to play it from another zone. 420.1.a 420.3.b Replacing Gangplank's return does not stop Transpositionist's next instruction because it refers to Gangplank and his might, not whether the return happened. 359.3.e.14.a 359.3.e.14.b 407.5 Gangplank remains on the board and remains a legal target, so the ability can still read his might. 359.3.e.12.a It reads that value when the later instruction executes, after the +3 increase applies. 359.3.f.2 An otherwise unmodified Gangplank has 9 at that point, so the unit must have less than 9 .

rulings.question: Does Vex, Apathetic's triggered ability target the unit that was just played?
rulings.answer: No. Vex's trigger condition identifies the unit that was just played, and the later word "it" refers back to that information. 383.2.a 359.3.f.3 Vex's controller never chooses among units, so the unit is not a target. 355.10.d 355.10.d.1 An ability that prevents enemy spells or abilities from choosing the unit therefore does not stop Vex from stunning it. 757 758 [Deflect] also adds no cost because Vex's ability does not choose the unit. 809.1.d

rulings.question: Does Vex, Apathetic stun a gear with Deploy at a battlefield when an opponent's Lady of Clockwork makes it a unit?
rulings.answer: No, Vex's ability does not trigger or stun an opponent's gear with [Deploy] at a battlefield when the opponent's Lady of Clockwork makes it a unit, even while Vex is at a battlefield. A card is played only when it finishes the process of playing a card in its entirety. 350 350.1 Lady of Clockwork's ability changes the chosen gear's card type at its current location instead of playing it. Because no unit was played, Vex's trigger condition is not met. 383.2.a 383.3

rulings.question: Can I move an opponent's unit after Vex, Apathetic says they can't move it?
rulings.answer: Yes, you can move the unit because Vex prevents the opponent identified by its trigger from moving it that turn, not every player. Vex's trigger condition identifies both the opponent who played the unit and the unit itself, so the later words "they" and "it" refer back to that information. 383.2.a 359.3.f.3 Charm , Void Assault , and Moonfall each instruct you to move an enemy unit. The player who performs a game action is responsible for it, even when another player controls the affected unit. 412.1 In each case, you perform the move, not the opponent who controls the unit, so Vex's restriction does not apply.

rulings.question: Does Vex, Cheerless increase the cost of enemy spells played from face down?
rulings.answer: Yes, while Vex is in combat, she adds to an enemy spell played from face down before discounts are applied. Playing a card from face down ignores its base cost, 811.1.b but Vex's increase is applied afterward. 356.1.b.3 Additional costs or other increases can raise the spell's cost further, and later discounts can reduce it. 356.2 356.3 356.4 This increase does not apply to units or gear played from face down because Vex modifies only spell costs.

rulings.question: Does Vex, Cheerless reduce Deflect costs when I play spells?
rulings.answer: Yes, while Vex is in combat, her discount applies to [Deflect] costs when your spell targets an opponent's permanent. [Deflect] is a mandatory additional cost. 356.2.a.2 When your spell targets an opponent's permanent with [Deflect], that additional cost is added before Vex's discount is applied. 809.1.d 356.2 356.4 Vex's discount can offset resources added by [Deflect] because discounts can reduce additional costs. 356.4.f Vex's discount cannot reduce the spell's cost below Vex's printed minimum of , but another total-cost discount applied afterward can reduce it further. 356.4.d.1 356.4.e

rulings.question: How do I perform Drakehound Packmaster's reveal instruction with one Void Hatchling?
rulings.answer: For each opponent's main deck, look at its current top card and choose whether to recycle it, then reveal the card now on top. Void Hatchling replaces Drakehound Packmaster 's reveal instruction with that sequence. 370.1.b If Drakehound Packmaster reveals from several opponents' decks at once, each deck's reveal is treated separately for replacement effects. 373 One Void Hatchling can apply across all of those events in the same replacement sequence. 373.2 Drakehound Packmaster then continues with the cards it revealed.

rulings.question: How do I perform Drakehound Packmaster's reveal instruction with three Void Hatchlings?
rulings.answer: For each opponent's main deck, apply the three replacement effects one at a time, making three separate look-and-recycle choices before revealing the card currently on top. Each replacement changes Drakehound Packmaster 's reveal into a look at the current top card, an optional recycle, and another reveal. 370.1.b When several replacement effects apply, they are ordered and applied one at a time. 372 After one copy applies, it cannot apply again to the original reveal or any event that replaced it. 370.2 The reveal created by that copy can still be replaced by another copy, so all three apply in sequence. 370.1.b 370.2 If Drakehound Packmaster reveals from several opponents' decks at once, each deck's reveal is treated separately. 373 Each Void Hatchling can apply across all of those events in one replacement sequence. 373.2 Each time, look only at the current top card and choose whether to recycle it. If you leave it on top, the next replacement looks at the same card; if you recycle it, the next replacement looks at the new top card. You never look at more than one card at a time or reorder any cards left on top. After the third replacement, reveal the current top card and continue Drakehound Packmaster's instructions normally.

rules.c: Golden and Silver Rules
Golden Rule
Card text supersedes rules text. Whenever a card fundamentally contradicts the rules, the card's indication is what is true.
Silver Rule
Card text uses different terminology than rules. Card text should be interpreted according to these rules, not as though it were text within these rules.

*Card,* when written in card effects, is shorthand for "*Main Deck* card." Runes, legends, and battlefields are *not* considered cards when executing the abilities and effects of game objects. They are considered cards for the purposes of these rules.
Cards refer to themselves in the first person.
* Units and legends say "I," "me," etc.
* Gear and spells say "this."
* Battlefields say "here."
* Cards may refer to themselves by their name for clarity. This is shorthand for the above terms.
“Can’t beats Can”
Cards that forbid actions or effects, as a broad method of determination, supersede cards that allow or permit that same action or effect.
If a card specifies that an action can “only” be performed under certain circumstances, it cannot be performed under any other circumstances.
When executing card text, do as much as you can, ignoring impossible instructions.
If all of a card’s instructions are impossible, it is still played and resolved, but nothing happens.
Cards a player owns may never be placed into a non-Board zone belonging to another player.
Non-Board zones corresponding to a player include Main Deck, Rune Deck, Trash, Hand, Chosen Champion zone, and Banishment.
If a card would enter such a zone, it goes to its owner’s corresponding zone instead.
Game Concepts
Deck Construction
*Riftbound* is a Trading Card Game where a player must provide their own cards to play against other players.

To play *Riftbound*, a player must have a *Main Deck,* a *Rune Deck,* a *Champion Legend*, and a number of *Battlefields* determined by the *Mode of Play.* These are collectively referred to as a player’s deck.

Cards in a player’s deck or rules of a *Game Mode* may indicate additional choices to be made while building the deck.
  *Example:* A unit reads in part “If [Name] is in your deck, choose 3 different legends in addition to your starting legend.” This decision is made while building the deck.
  *Example:* The rules of a game mode read in part “Choose an additional Chosen Champion with a different Champion Tag and Domain than your Champion Legend. Place it in the Champion Zone at the start of the game alongside your other Chosen Champion. Your deck’s Domain Identity includes that additional Chosen Champion’s Domain, if applicable.” The Chosen Champion chosen this way is decided while building the deck.
1 *Champion Legend*
This is placed in the *Legend Zone* at the start of the game.
This will dictate the *Domain Identity* of the deck.
Cards included in your deck must abide by your *Domain Identity.*
Your deck’s *Domain Identity* is dictated by the domains of your *Champion Legend.* In the default card frame, these domains appear as symbols in the legend’s upper left corner.
If a card has a single *Domain*, then that card is permitted in the *Domain Identity* that corresponds to the same *Domain.*
If a card has more than one *Domain*, then that card is permitted *only* in a *Domain Identity* that contains all of the indicated *Domains* on that card.
If a card has no *Domain,* then that card is permitted in decks of any *Domain Identity.*

Some *Game Effects* may allow a player to add cards to their deck irrespective of those cards’ *Domains.* Those cards are considered part of their deck’s *Domain Identity,* regardless of their *Domain.*
*A Main Deck of at least 40 cards:* A Chosen Champion Unit, as well as Units, Gear, and Spells
*Chosen Champion*
This will be placed in the *Champion Zone* at the start of the game.

Must be a champion unit with a champion tag that matches the tag on your *Champion Legend.*
  *Example:* Loose Cannon has the tag *Jinx*. Therefore, a player could choose Jinx, Rebel or Jinx, Demolitionist as their Chosen Champion, because they also have the tag *Jinx*.
  *Example:* Tibbers has the tag *Annie*, but it is a signature unit, not a champion unit. It cannot be your Chosen Champion, even if your Champion Legend has the tag *Annie*.

A player’s *Chosen Champion* is both the specific card chosen for this slot during Deck Building and also any *Champion Unit* with the same name as the specific card selected for this specific slot during the course of play.
  *Example:* A player chose Jinx, Rebel as their Chosen Champion. One copy of Jinx, Rebel starts the game in their Chosen Champion zone. Any additional copies of Jinx, Rebel in their Main Deck, their hand, their trash, or on the board also count as their Chosen Champion for any game rules and effects that care about Chosen Champion status during the game.
Your *Main Deck* can include up to 3 copies of the same named card.

This includes your *Chosen Champion.*
  *Example:* A deck could include Volibear, Furious as its Chosen Champion and still include 2 more copies of Volibear, Furious in their Main Deck.

Cards have different names even if they represent the same character.
  *Example:* A deck could include 3 copies of Yasuo, Remorseful and 3 copies of Yasuo, Windrider, because they have different names.
Subject to *Domain Identity.*
Your deck may only contain 3 *total Signature* cards that have the same Champion tag as your *Champion Legend.*
Regardless of name, a deck may only contain a sum total of 3 Signature cards.
All of the Signature cards must have the Champion tag that corresponds to the *Champion Legend* of the deck.
Signature cards are not Champion units and cannot be placed in the *Champion Zone*.
Subject to card legality of the *Format* being played.
*Rune Deck*
12 *Rune Cards*
Cards in the *Rune Deck* must be of the *Domain Identity* of your *Champion Legend.*
Must be shuffled and kept separate from the *Main Deck.*
*Battlefields*
The number will be dictated by your *Mode of Play.*
Subject to *Domain Identity* if applicable.
Cannot include more than one of a *Battlefield* of the same name when there are more than one required for the deck.
Setup
Spaces
The *Play Area* is a collection of logical *Zones* that are defined by their behaviors and relationships to *Players.* These *Zones* are grouped into *The Board* and *Non-Board Zones.*
*The Board*
*Bases*
Each player has their own *Base.*

Each Base is a *Location.*
  *See rule 197. Locations for more information.*
*Permanents* and *Runes* controlled by a player reside in that player's *Base.*
*Permanents* attached to *Permanents* controlled by a player may also be found in that player’s *Base,* regardless of their controller.
*Permanents* and *Runes* in *Bases* are *Public Information.*
*Battlefield Zone*
The *Battlefield Zone* houses multiple *Battlefields.*

Each *Battlefield* is individually a *Location.*
  *See rule 197. Locations for more information.*
*Battlefields* and permanents at *Battlefields* are *Public Information.*
*Facedown Zones*
Each Battlefield is associated with a sub-zone called a *Facedown Zone*, a single logical space that a card can be put facedown in through various *Game Effects.*
Each *Facedown Zone* has a maximum occupancy of one card.
The maximum occupancy of a *Facedown Zone* can increase or decrease.

If the maximum occupancy of a *Facedown Zone* decreases to a number less than the number of cards currently located there, the controller of that *Facedown Zone* must put a number of cards equal to the difference in the trash from the *Facedown Zone.*
Cards can only be placed in or occupy the *Facedown Zone* if the controller of the card also controls the associated *Battlefield.*

If a player loses *Control* of a *Battlefield*, any cards in the *Facedown Zone* associated with that *Battlefield* are removed during the next *Cleanup.*
  *See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.*
  *See rule 422. Hide for more information.*
Facedown Zones are not locations.
Facedown Zones are *Public Zones,* though facedown cards located there are *Private.*
*Legend Zone*
The space for each player's *Champion Legend.*
This is not a location.

The *Champion Legend* here is a *Game Object.*
  *See rule 119. Game Objects for more information.*
The *Champion Legend* cannot be removed, moved, or displaced from this zone.
Some effects may add a legend card or token to the *Legend Zone.* These legends are not *Champion Legends.*
Non-Champion legends may be removed from the Legend Zone. They cannot exist in any zone other than the Legend Zone or *Banishment.*
*Non-Board Zones*
*The Chain*

Cards and abilities are placed here as part of the process of being *played.*
  *See rule 327. Chains for more information.*
Cards and abilities on the *Chain* are *Public Information.*
*Trashes*
Each player has their own *Trash.*
This space is where cards are placed when they are killed or discarded, when they finish being executed as spells, when they are moved to the trash as an effect, etc.
Cards in each player’s *Trash* are *unordered.* Their sequence does not matter, and they may be reorganized.

Cards in a player's *Trash* are *Public Information.*
  *See rule 128. Privacy for more information.*
*Champion Zones*
Each player has their own *Champion Zone.*
The space each player puts their *Chosen Champion* at the start of the game.
The *Chosen Champion* cannot be returned to this zone by normal means.
If a *Chosen Champion* is instructed to be returned to this zone, it can only do so if there is not a card already in this zone.

The *Chosen Champion* can be played from here as normal, following the rules of *Playing a Card.*
  *See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.*
Cards in a player’s *Champion Zone* are *Public Information.*
*Main Deck Zones*
Each player has their own *Main Deck Zone.*
The space for the player's *Main Deck.*
Primarily houses the face-down *Main Deck* during gameplay.
The number of cards in a player’s *Main Deck* is *Public Information.*

The order of cards in the *Main Deck* is *Secret Information* during the course of play.
  *See rule 128. Privacy for more information.*
*Rune Deck Zones*
Each player has their own *Rune Deck Zone.*
The space for the player's *Rune Deck.*
Primarily houses the face-down runes during gameplay.
