Ignoring Effects
Some Game Effects may instruct players to ignore abilities while performing a game action or procedure.

Any abilities ignored in this way are treated as inactive for the purposes of the game action or procedure.
  *Example:* A spell reads “Ignore Deflect while paying this spell’s costs.” Any instances of the Deflect keyword on relevant units are treated as inactive while paying the costs of the spell.
  *Example:* A unit reads “You ignore Backline while assigning combat damage here.” While assigning combat damage in the combat damage step with this unit present, any instances of Backline on enemy units is treated as inactive. The unit’s controller can assign damage to any units with Backline as if they didn’t have it.

Ignored abilities are only treated as inactive for the specific game action or procedure described, and only by the players directed by the ability.
  *Example:* A spell reads in part “Ignore Deflect while paying this spell’s costs.” If another player attempts to play a spell targeting the same units that the above spell does, that other spell will not ignore Deflect.
  *Example:* A unit reads “You ignore Backline while assigning combat damage here.” Any other player assigning combat damage at the same location as that unit will not be able to ignore Backline.
Keywords
A *Keyword* is a specific term that appears on *Cards* that acts as a shorthand for a specific game effect, or *ability* of any variety.
A *Keyword* can be an ability.
*Keywords* can be identified by having a *colored highlight* behind them.
The color of the highlight has no effect on gameplay.
*Keywords* can be referenced or specified by other *Game Effects.*
Other effects may grant *Keywords.*
The definition and rules of the specific *Keyword* will determine the behavior if a *Keyword* is granted while it is already present.
The effect that granted the *Keyword* will specify the duration for which it is granted.
If an effect that grants a *Keyword* does not specify a duration, the duration is as long as that *Game Object* remains on *the Board* or in its current *Non-Board Zone.*
Other effects may remove *Keywords.*
The effect that removed the *Keyword* will specify the duration it is removed.
If an effect that removes a *Keyword* does not specify a duration, the duration is as long as that *Game Object* remains on *the Board* or in its current *Non-Board Zone.*
A card can have any number of *Keywords.*
Similar to other rules text, execute any effects of *Keywords* in the order listed when reading the card from top to bottom of the rules text.
Keyword Glossary
*Accelerate*
*Accelerate* is an *Optional Additional Cost* keyword.
*Accelerate* is present on *Units.*
*Accelerate* is functionally short for "As you play me, you may pay [1][C] as an additional cost. If you do, I enter ready."
If the unit has one or more domains, the Power portion of the *Accelerate* cost can be paid only with a Power that matches one of the domains of the unit.
If the unit has no domain, the Power portion of the *Accelerate* cost can be paid with [A] (a Power of any domain).
*Accelerate* is an *Optional Additional Cost* to be paid as a player plays the unit with the ability.
*Accelerate* costs cannot be paid while the unit is on the board, only as part of the steps of playing a card.

Paying the cost generates a *Delayed Replacement Effect.* Even if the unit loses the *Accelerate* keyword during the finalization process, as long as the cost was paid, that unit will still enter ready.
*Accelerate* has no function while on the board.
Multiple instances of *Accelerate* are redundant.
*Accelerate,* and whether or not a unit has *Accelerate,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Accelerate* generates a delayed replacement effect that replaces a unit entering the board exhausted with it entering ready. It does not enter exhausted and then become ready.
*Accelerate* will not interact with, or trigger, abilities that are affected by units becoming ready.
*Action*
*Action* is a *Permissive* keyword.
It is present on *Cards, Rune Abilities, Legend Abilities* or *Permanent Abilities.*
*Action* grants the corresponding card or effect permission to be played or activated during *Showdowns,* even when it is not the Controlling player's turn.
*Action* is functionally short for the following:
On Cards: "This can be played during showdowns on any player's turn."
On Activated Abilities: "This can be activated during showdowns on any player's turn."
*Action* is formatted as “[Action]” on spells, or “[Action][>]” on abilities.
The card or effect with this keyword is not restricted to showdowns. This permission is inclusive of all other timings and options available to the ability as written or by default.

*Action* does not alter the function of any instruction of the corresponding card or effect it is on. It is *only* permission.
  *Example:* Playing a Unit with Action still has the inherent restrictions of playing Units without Action. It can only be played to the controlling player's base or a battlefield they control.
Some passive abilities may grant a card or ability *Action* under certain conditions. The card or ability does not have the *Action* keyword unless and until those circumstances are true.

Those conditions might only be fulfilled while the card or ability is on the chain. In such a case, it can still be played or activated at the appropriate timing as long as doing so *could* fulfill the conditions.

If the chain item does not fulfill the conditions by the time step 5: check legality has been reached, the actions taken while playing it are undone and it is returned to the zone it was played from if it is a card.
Action is a referenceable characteristic.
Whether or not a *Game Object* has *Action* is a characteristic of that *Game Object* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
Whether or not a *Spell* has *Action* is a characteristic of that *Spell* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
Whether or not an *Ability* has *Action* is a characteristic of that *Ability* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Assault*
*Assault* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is present on *Units.*
*Assault* is formatted as "Assault [X]".
The X is referenced in the functional text of the ability.
The X is referred to as the *Assault Value.*
If X is omitted, it is presumed to be 1.
It is functionally short for "While I am an attacker, I have +X [M]."

Being an attacker means the *Unit* has gained the *Attacker* designation during *Combat.*
  *See rule 461. Combat for more information.*
*Assault* remains in effect as long as the *Unit* maintains the *Attacker* designation.

If a Unit has *Assault* or has been granted *Assault* and is granted *Assault* by an additional source, the *Assault Value* of all granted *Assault* keywords is summed.
  *Example:* Petty Officer has Assault. It is chosen as the target of Cleave, which says "Give a unit [Assault 3] this turn." After Cleave resolves, Petty Officer has Assault 4 this turn.
*Assault,* and whether or not a unit has *Assault,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Deathknell*
*Deathknell* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
It is present on *Permanents.*
It is formatted as "[Deathknell][>] [Effect]".
[Effect] is the rules text for the specific instance of *Deathknell.* This is referred to as the *Deathknell* effect.
It is functionally short for "When I die, [Effect]."
[Effect] is the rules text of the *Deathknell* effect.
[Effect] may be written in the past tense. In doing so, it refers to the moment the *Deathknell* trigger was added to the chain, not any previous moment.
The Trigger for this and similar effects that trigger on their source’s death is the Permanent being *Killed* and sent to the *Trash.*

If the Permanent with the effect is not sent to the *Trash*, for example because its"killed" event was replaced with a recall, the triggered ability will be removed from the chain.
  *Example:* Draven, Audacious is killed in combat. Draven reads in part “When I die in combat, choose an opponent. They gain 1 point.” Draven’s controller has a Zhonya’s Hourglass in base. Draven’s death is replaced by him being healed, recalled, and exhausted. Draven’s triggered ability will be removed from the chain.
The trigger will be added to the chain as a *Pending Item* before the card with an ability that triggers on its own death is moved to the trash due to a *Kill* instruction or a *Cleanup.*
Before the card is moved to the *Trash*, note its location, its attributes, and any other details related to the effect of its triggered ability to process the trigger after it has been *Finalized*.
Each instance of *Deathknell* a Permanent may have will trigger separately.
The controller will choose the order to add these *Triggers* to the chain.
*Deathknell,* and whether or not a permanent has *Deathknell,* is a characteristic of the permanent and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Deflect*
*Deflect* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is normally present on Permanents.
It is formatted as "Deflect [X]".
The X is referenced in the functional text of the ability.
The X is referred to as the *Deflect Value.*
If X is omitted, it is presumed to be 1.

It is functionally short for "Spells and abilities an opponent controls that target [me/this] cost an amount of Power equal to [Deflect Value] more to play as an additional cost for each time they choose [me/this]."

The Power used to pay this cost may always be of any Domain.
  *Example:* A Fury spell targets an Order unit with Deflect. The Power used to pay the Deflect cost can be any Domain; it does not need to match the Domain of the spell or the target.

It is an effect that imposes a *Mandatory Additional Cost* on Spells and Abilities that choose the *Game Object* that has this ability.
  *See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.*
If a *Game Object* has *Deflect,* or has been granted *Deflect,* and is granted *Deflect* by an additional source, the *Deflect Value* of all granted *Deflect* keywords is summed.
*Deflect,* and whether or not a *Game Object* has *Deflect,* is a characteristic of the permanent and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Ganking*
*Ganking* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is present on Units.
It is functionally short for "I may move to a battlefield from another battlefield with a standard move."
It is a passive ability that adds permissions to the Unit's Standard Move.
It does not restrict or remove options from the Unit's Standard Move.
It does not have an activation cost.
It does not give additional abilities or activations of Movement, only new options for the Standard Move.
Multiple instances of *Ganking* are redundant.
*Ganking,* and whether or not a unit has *Ganking,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Hidden*
*Hidden* is a keyword that acts as a prerequisite to perform the *Hide* Discretionary Action.
It is present on Spells, Units, and Gear.

It is functionally short for "While this card is in your hand or in your Champion Zone on your turn during an Open State, you may pay [A] to hide this facedown at a battlefield you control that doesn't already have a facedown card hidden there for as long as you control that battlefield. Beginning on the next turn, this gains [Reaction] and you may play this, ignoring its base cost."
It allows the player to take the Discretionary Action *Hide*.
Hide is not a subset of *Play*.
Hiding a card does not open a chain.
Playing a card from facedown (or "from Hidden") does open a chain.

Some choices made while playing a card from facedown are restricted to the battlefield where it was hidden. A card cannot be played from facedown if it is a spell with no valid targets under these restrictions.
  *See rule 355.6. Targeting for more information.*
A hidden permanent must be played to that battlefield.
This includes hidden gear, and overrides the normal restriction that gear have in only being allowed to be played to base.

If a hidden spell chooses any targets, those targets must be chosen from among options at the battlefield it was played from, unless it explicitly restricts targeting in such a way that makes this impossible.
  *Example:* Emperor’s Divide is a spell with hidden that reads in part “Move any number of friendly units at a battlefield to their base.” When this spell is played from facedown, all units chosen for the spell must be located at the same battlefield it was played from.

If a play effect of a hidden permanent chooses any targets, those targets must be chosen from among options at the battlefield it was played to, unless the ability explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible.
  *Example:* Blastcone Fae is a unit with Hidden and “When you play me, give a unit -2 [M] this turn, to a minimum of 1 [M].” Because this is a play effect, its target must be chosen from among units at the battlefield it was played to if Blastcone Fae was played from facedown.
  *Example:* Tideturner is a unit with Hidden and “When you play me, you may choose a unit you control at another location. Move me to its location and it to my original location.” Because its play effect has a targeting restriction that can never be fulfilled by a unit at its battlefield, its target may be chosen freely from among the available options.
  *Example:* A spell reads in part “The next unit you play this turn can be played to any battlefield.” After playing that spell, a player plays Blastcone Fae from facedown to a battlefield other than the one where it was hidden. Blastcone Fae’s play effect must choose targets from among units at the battlefield Blastcone Fae was played to, not the one it was played from.

A play effect of a permanent played from facedown references information from its source when determining what battlefield it was played from and what targets are legal.
  *Example:* A unit reads in part “When you play me, kill another friendly unit.” If it is played from the facedown zone, the play effect must choose a friendly unit at the battlefield the unit was played from. If the unit is no longer on the board when the play effect attempts to finalize, it will not be able to choose a legal target. If the unit is no longer on the board when the play effect attempts to resolve, the play effect will not be able to reference the information of where the unit was played from, and it will mistarget.

Each target is treated separately and individually when processing this rule.
  *Example:* Smoke and Mirrors is a spell that reads in part “Choose a unit you control and another unit you control at a different location.” If Smoke and Mirrors is played from facedown, the first unit chosen can be chosen at the battlefield Smoke and Mirrors was played from, so it must be. The second unit chosen explicitly restricts targeting in a way that makes this impossible, so it can be chosen from any location.
If a hidden spell or a play effect of a hidden permanent causes you to play a unit, you must choose to play that unit at that battlefield.

Abilities and instructions of hidden cards other than the choices listed above function as normal.
  *Example:* Stand United is a spell that has Hidden and says “Buff a friendly unit. Buffs give an additional +1 might to friendly units this turn.” If it’s played from facedown, the first part of its ability must choose a friendly unit at the same battlefield, but the second part of its ability affects all friendly units with buffs, no matter where they are.
Instead of being hidden, a card with *Hidden* may be played for its cost as normal, at its normal timing with no restrictions on targeting.
Multiple instances of Hidden are redundant.
*Hidden,* and whether or not a card has *Hidden,* is a characteristic of the card and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
This is true as long as the card is not facedown. A facedown card is not a card with *Hidden.*
A card that is *Hidden* gains *Reaction* the turn after it is hidden while facedown or played from facedown, and may be played any time a card with *Reaction* may be played as a result.
The property is granted to the card in its facedown state, and is not publicly known.
*Legion*
*Legion* is a *Dependent Keyword.*
It is formatted as "[Legion][>] [Text]".
Starting from the Keyword to the end of the clause, the entire statement is the *Legion Ability*.
*Legion* is functionally short for “If you have played another card this turn, this card gains [Text].”
The [Text] is the *Dependent Ability.*
As long as a card different than the one with the *Legion* ability has been *Finalized* by you on the same turn then the *Dependent Ability* is *Active* on the card with *Legion.*

All instances of *Legion* on cards a player controls are satisfied by that player playing a single card.
  *Example:* One card has three different Legion Abilities. The Legion Text of all three abilities will be active as long as one card has been finalized by the card's controller earlier in the same turn.
*Legion*, and whether or not a card has *Legion*, is a characteristic of the card and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Reaction*
*Reaction* is a *Permissive* keyword.
It can be present on *Cards, Rune Abilities, Legend Abilities* and *Permanent Abilities.*
*Reaction* grants the corresponding card or effect all abilities and permissions of *Action.*
*Reaction*, additionally, is functionally short for the following:
On Cards: "This can be played during *Closed States* on any player's turn."
On Activated Abilities: "This can be activated during *Closed States* on any player's turn."
*Reaction* is formatted as “[Reaction]” on cards, or “[Reaction][>]” on abilities.

The corresponding card or effect with this keyword is not restricted to *Closed States* or *Showdowns*. This permission is inclusive of all other timings and options available to the ability as written, Action's permissions, or by default.
*Reaction* does not alter the function of any instruction of the Card, Rune, or Effect it is on. It is *only* Permission.
Playing *Units* with *Reaction* still has the inherent restrictions of playing *Units* without *Reaction.* It can only be played to the controlling player's base or a battlefield they control.
Some passive abilities may grant a card or ability *Reaction* under certain conditions. The card or ability does not have the *Reaction* keyword unless and until those circumstances are true.

Those conditions might only be fulfilled while the card or ability is on the chain. In such a case, it can still be played or activated at the appropriate timing as long as doing so *could* fulfill the conditions.

If the chain item does not fulfill the conditions by the time step 5: check legality has been reached, the actions taken while playing it are undone and it is returned to the zone it was played from if it is a card.
*Reaction* is a referencable characteristic.
Whether or not a *Game Object* has *Reaction* is a characteristic of that *Game Object* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
Whether or not a *Spell* has *Reaction* is a characteristic of that *Spell* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
Whether or not an *Ability* has *Reaction* is a characteristic of that *Ability* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Shield*
*Shield* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is present on Units.
*Shield* is formatted as "Shield [X]".
The X is referenced in the functional text of the ability.
The X is referred to as the *Shield Value.*
If X is omitted, it is presumed to be 1.
It is functionally short for "While I am a defender, I have +X [M]."

Being a defender means the *Unit* has gained the *Defender* designation during *Combat.*
  *See rule 461. Combat for more information.*
*Shield* remains in effect as long as the *Unit* maintains the *Defender* designation.

If a *Unit* has *Shield,* or has been granted *Shield,* and is granted *Shield* by an additional source, the *Shield Value* of all granted *Shield* keywords is summed.
  *Example:* Stalwart Poro has Shield. It is chosen as the target of Block, which says "Give a unit [Shield 3] and [Tank] this turn." After Block resolves, Stalwart Poro has Shield 4 this turn.
*Shield,* and whether or not a unit has *Shield,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Tank*
*Tank* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is present on Units.
It is functionally short for "I must be assigned lethal damage before any other unit with the same controller as me that does not have [Tank] during the Combat Damage step."
It alters how players can elect to assign combat damage during combat.
Players must still assign lethal damage to a unit before moving to the next when assigning their damage.

If more than one unit with *Tank* is present with the same controller in Combat, damage may be assigned to any of them. Units without *Tank* are invalid assignments until all units with *Tank* have lethal damage assigned to them.
Multiple instances of *Tank* are redundant.
*Tank,* and whether or not a unit has *Tank,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Temporary*
*Temporary* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
It is present on Permanents.
It is functionally short for "At the start of this permanent's controller's Beginning Phase, before scoring, kill this."
The Trigger Condition is the controller of the permanent's Beginning Phase starting.
Multiple instances of *Temporary* are redundant.
Regardless of how many instances there are, the ability will only trigger once.
*Temporary,* and whether or not a permanent has *Temporary,* is a characteristic of the permanent and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Vision*
*Vision* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
It is present on Permanents.
It is functionally short for "When this is played, [Predict].”
The trigger is the permanent entering the Board.
Multiple instances of *Vision* trigger separately.
The player may choose to recycle or not recycle for each instance of *Vision* separately.
If the player does not recycle the top card and nothing else happens in between the triggers resolving, each instance of *Vision* will see the same card.
*Vision,* and whether or not a permanent has *Vision,* is a characteristic of the permanent and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Equip*
*Equip* is an *Activated Ability* keyword.
*Equip* is present on *Gear* with the tag *Equipment.*
*Equip* has a cost to activate and *Attaches* the card with *Equip* to a chosen *Unit* when the cost is paid.
*Equip’s* choice is a *Target.*
The chosen *Unit* will become the *Top-Most Card* for the *Attach* action.
*Equip* is formatted as “*Equip* [Cost]”

If paying costs or making choices for this ability causes triggered abilities to trigger, they will be placed on the chain above this ability in a *Pending* state.
  *See rule 376. Activated Abilities for more information.*
*Equip* is functionally short for “[Cost]: *Attach* this gear to a unit you control.”
*Equip* costs may include both resource costs and non-resource costs.
*Equip* abilities may also include text that alters the *Equip* cost. Such text is taken into account when determining a card’s *Equip* cost when paying for the ability.
*Equip* abilities may include text that alters the timing or targeting of the *Equip* ability.
When the *Attach* action completes from this keyword, the *Unit* that was chosen is considered to have been *Equipped* by the *Gear* with this ability.
This is an event other *Game Effects* and *Triggered Abilities* can reference.
*Equipped* is the state of a *Top-Most Card* being *Attached* by one or more cards that are *Equipment.*
The state of being *Equipped* is synchronous with that of the *Attached* state of the *Equipment.*
A *Top-Most Card* is *Equipped* as long as one or more of its *Attached* cards are *Equipment.*
The state of being *Equipped* corresponds to a *Top-Most card* having a card with *Equip* that is *Attached* to it.
Multiple instances of *Equip* are equivalent to multiple *Activated Abilities* and can each be activated separately by paying the corresponding costs.
*Equip,* and whether or not a *Gear* has *Equip,* is a characteristic of the Gear and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*

Whether or not a *Gear* has *Equip* may be referenced even if the *Rules Text* of the *Gear* is *Inactive.*
  *See rule 716. Attachment for more information.*
*Quick-Draw*
*Quick-Draw* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword. It is also a *Permissive* keyword.
*Quick-Draw* is present on *Gear* with *Equip* abilities.
Cards with *Quick-Draw* have *Reaction* inherently.
*Quick-Draw* allows cards to be played and *Attached* using *Reaction* timing.

*Quick-Draw* is functionally short for “*[Reaction]*” and “When you play this, *attach* it to a *Unit* you control.”
  *See rule 716. Attachment for more information.*
Multiple instances of *Quick-Draw* do not trigger separately and have no effect beyond the first.
*Quick-Draw*, and whether or not a gear has *Quick-Draw*, is a characteristic of the Gear and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Repeat*
*Repeat* is an *Optional Additional Cost* keyword.
*Repeat* is present on *Spells* and *Abilities.*
*Repeat* is an optional cost that a player may pay to execute the effect of their spells and abilities a second time.
*Repeat* is formatted as “*Repeat* [Cost]”
The Cost is an *Additional Cost* to be paid during the steps of playing the spell or ability.
If a spell or ability has more than one instance of *Repeat*, each Cost may be paid or not paid individually.
Each *Repeat Cost* can be paid only a single time.
*Repeat* is functionally short for “You may pay *[Cost]* as an additional cost as you play this. If you do, execute the instructions of this chain item one additional time during resolution.”

When the additional cost is paid, the effect of the spell or ability, upon resolution, will be performed an additional time.
  *Example: Desert’s Call is a spell with [Repeat] [2] and “Play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token.” If its controller pays its Repeat cost as they play it, the card’s instruction to play a Sand Soldier is executed twice, as though the card says “Play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token. Play a 2 [M] Sand Soldier unit token.”*
  *Example:* A unit reads in part “When I attack or defend, you may deal damage equal to my Might to an enemy unit here,” and “My abilities have [Repeat] — Discard 1.” When its ability triggers, if its controller pays the Repeat cost as they play it, the ability’s instruction to deal damage equal to the unit’s Might is executed twice, as though the ability says “Deal damage equal to my Might to an enemy unit here. Deal damage equal to my Might to an enemy unit here.”
Any instructions not performed on resolution of the spell or ability are ignored.

When a spell or ability’s effect is performed an additional time with *Repeat*, choices must be made at the usual time during the *Make Relevant Choices* step of *Playing a Card.*
  *See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.*

Choices made for the additional execution do not have to be the same as the choices made for the initial execution.
  *Example:* Rocket Barrage is a spell with [Repeat] [4][C] and “Choose one —
  Deal 4 to a unit in a base. [or] Kill a gear.” If Rocket Barrage’s controller pays its Repeat cost as they play it, they may choose the same mode or a different one, and if they choose the same mode, may choose the same target or a different one. If they choose “Kill a gear” twice and choose two different gear, they must specify which gear is the first target and which is the second. As the spell resolves, those two gear will be killed in the chosen order.
Multiple instances of *Repeat* can be paid for separately. The spell or ability’s instructions will be executed an additional time on resolution for each instance of *Repeat* that is paid for.
Regardless of the number of times a spell or ability's instructions are executed with this keyword, it is only *Played* once.
*Repeat*, and whether or not a spell or ability has *Repeat*, is a characteristic of the spell or ability and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Weaponmaster*
*Weaponmaster* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
*Weaponmaster* is present on *Units.*

*Weaponmaster* is a *Play Effect* that chooses an *Equipment* you control and allows you to pay its *Equip* cost at a discount, regardless of the usual timing of the *Equip* ability, to *Attach* that *Equipment* to the unit with *Weaponmaster.*

*Weaponmaster* is functionally short for: “When you play me, you may choose a *Card* you control with the *Equipment* tag. Necessary portions of its *Rules Text* are no longer Inactive if they are currently *Inactive.* Pay the cost of its *Equip* ability, reduced by [A], to attach it to this unit.”
  *See rule 716. Attachment for more information.*
*Weaponmaster* can choose an *Equipment* whether it has an *Equip* ability or not.

The cost of the *Equip* ability is determined as though that *Equip* ability was being activated choosing the unit with the *Weaponmaster* ability, as modulated by any abilities that alter *Equip* costs.

The *Equip* ability is not actually activated when its cost is determined in this way. An effect that grants an activated ability a cost reduction when it is played will not apply to the *Equip* cost calculated during the resolution of a *Weaponmaster* trigger, because the *Equip* ability is not actually played.

Effects that reduce the cost of *Equip* abilities without referring to those abilities being played, or the *Equip* ability being referenced in specific, will be included when calculating costs in this way.
If the chosen card’s *Equip* cost does not contain [A], it can still be paid, but will not be reduced.
If the chosen card doesn’t have an *Equip* cost, it can’t be paid.

If the chosen card’s *Equip* cost can’t be paid, if it can’t be detached from its current *Top-Most* card, or if it can’t be attached to the unit with the *Weaponmaster* ability, it stays in its current location, *Attached* to anything it was already *Attached* to.
The *Equip* ability is not activated this way, and the unit with the *Weaponmaster* ability is not chosen.
Multiple instances of *Weaponmaster* trigger separately, and can choose different targets.
If you choose the same target with multiple instances of *Weaponmaster*, each will resolve separately.
*Weaponmaster* has no function while on the board.
*Weaponmaster*, and whether or not a unit has *Weaponmaster*, is a characteristic of the *Unit* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Ambush*
*Ambush* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is normally present on *Units*.
It is functionally short for "I may be played to a battlefield where you control *Units*" and “I have [*Reaction*] as long as I’m being played to a battlefield where you control *Units*.”

It is a passive ability that adds options to locations that are valid for a *Unit* to be played to during the Make Relevant Choices step of Playing a Card
  *See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information*

*Ambush* can also appear as a verb on a card. In such a case, the verb is taken to mean “play with the permissions of the *Ambush* keyword.”
  *Example:* Rengar, Trophy Hunter reads in part “I can [Ambush] to a battlefield where there are enemy units, even if you don't have units there.” This ability expands the normal permissions of the Ambush keyword to include battlefields where there are enemy units.
  *Example:* A card reads in part “Opponents can only [Ambush] at any time they could play cards with [Action].” This ability introduces a restriction to when opponents can play cards with Ambush.
Multiple instances of *Ambush* are redundant.
If there are no units at the location chosen before *Finalization* completes for any reason, then it is no longer a valid location by *Ambush*’s reasoning and cannot be played there
Other effects and permissions may still enable this *Unit* to be able to be played to the selected location, but *Ambush’s* permission will not be valid
*Ambush*, and whether or not a unit has *Ambush*, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Hunt*
*Hunt* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
*Hunt* is present on *Units.*
*Hunt* is both a *Conquer* and a *Hold* effect.
*Hunt* is formatted as “*Hunt* X”

*Hunt* is functionally short for: “When I *Conquer* or *Hold*, my controller gains X XP.”
  *See rule 728. XP for more information*
If X is omitted, it is presumed to be 1.
X is referred to as the *Hunt Value.*
If a Unit has *Hunt*, or has been granted *Hunt*, and is granted *Hunt* by an additional source, the *Hunt Value* of all granted *Hunt* keywords is summed.
*Hunt*, and whether or not a unit has *Hunt*, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Level*
*Level* is a *Dependent Keyword.*
It is formatted as "[Level [N][>] [Text]".
Starting from the Keyword to the end of the clause, the entire statement is the *Level Ability*.
It is functionally short for “While you have [N] or more XP, this card gains ‘[Text]’.”
The [Text] here is the *Dependent Ability*
As long as the controlling player has [N] XP, then the *Dependent Ability* will be be *Active* on the card with *Level*
If the controller of the card with *Level* changes, then the *Dependent Ability* will be rendered *Active* or *Inactive* based on the new controller’s XP.
The *Dependent Ability* will be *Inactive* as soon as the controlling player has less than [N] XP.
*Level,* and whether or not a card has *Level* is a characteristic of the card and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Unique*
*Unique* is a *Deck Constraint Permission.*
It is normally present on main deck cards.
*Unique* is not functionally short for any rules text, and instead provides a restriction to players during Deck Construction.
A deck can contain only one card of a given name if the card has *Unique*
If a card is a *Signature* card and is also *Unique*, then that deck can contain any combination of three *Signature* cards, but still only one of each named *Unique* card.
Cards with *Unique* have no additional effects during gameplay.
*Unique*, and whether or not a Card has *Unique*, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Backline*
*Backline* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
It is present on Units.
It is functionally short for “I must be assigned lethal damage after any other unit with the same controller as me that does not have [Backline] during the Combat Damage step.”
It alters how players can elect to assign combat damage during combat.
Players must still assign lethal damage to a unit before moving to the next when assigning their damage.

If more than one unit with Backline is present with the same controller in Combat, damage may be assigned to any of them. Units with Backline are invalid assignments until all units without Backline have lethal damage assigned to them.
Multiple Instances of Backline are redundant.
Backline, and whether or not a unit has Backline, is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Empower*
*Empower* is an *Activated Ability* keyword.
*Empower* is normally present on permanents and legends.

*Empower* has a cost to activate and *Empowers* the source of the ability when the cost is paid.
  *See rule 442. Empower (Game Action) for more information.*
The source game object is not a target of the *Empower* ability.
*Empower* is formatted as “*Empower* [Cost]”
*Empower* is functionally short for “[Cost]: *Empower* this. Play only if not Empowered.”
*Empower* costs may include both resource costs and non-resource costs.
*Empower* abilities may also include text that alters the *Empower* cost. Such text is taken into account when determining a card’s *Empower* cost for any reason.
*Empower* abilities may include text that alters the timing of the *Empower* ability.

*Game Objects* with *Empower* abilities may have or gain permissions to be *Empowered* multiple times. Such *Game Objects* ignore the normal “Play only if not Empowered.” restriction on *Empower* abilities.
When the *Empower* action completes from this keyword, the source permanent or legend becomes *Empowered.*
This is an event other *Game Effects* and *Triggered Abilities* can reference.
Multiple instances of *Empower* are equivalent to multiple activated abilities and can each be activated separately by paying the corresponding costs.
*Empower* and whether a permanent or legend has *Empower* are a characteristic of those *Game Objects* and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Empowered*
*Empowered* is a *Dependent Keyword.*
It is formatted as “[Empowered][>] [Text].”
Starting from the keyword to the end of the clause, the entire statement is the *Empowered Ability.*
It is functionally short for “While I have the *Empowered* status, this card gains ‘[Text]’.”
The [Text] here is the *Dependent Ability.*
As long as the *Game Object* has the *Empowered* status, then the *Dependent Ability* will be active.
If the *Dependent Ability* is a *Triggered Ability* whose condition is “When I become Empowered,” or a permutation thereof, it will be active and trigger when its source becomes *Empowered.*
*Empowered* and whether or not a card has an *Empowered Ability* is a characteristic of the card that may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Flow*
*Flow* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
*Flow* is present on *Spells.*
It is functionally short for “You may play this from your trash for its flow cost. Then banish it.”

Banishing the spell in this way is a delayed replacement effect. If the spell would leave the chain after becoming a finalized chain item, and leaving the chain wasn’t instructed by its own execution, banish it instead.
  *See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.*
  *See rule 390. Delayed Abilities for more information.*
Playing a spell for its *Flow* cost does not change the timing at which it can be played, nor any permissions for the spell aside from the zone from which it can be played.
*Flow* is formatted as “*Flow* [Cost]”
The cost is an alternate cost that replaces the base cost of the spell to be paid during finalization.
*Flow* costs may include both resource costs and non-resource costs.
If a spell has multiple instances of the *Flow* keyword with different costs, its controller may choose which cost to apply as they play it.
*Flow*, and whether or not a spell has *Flow*, is a characteristic of the Spell and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Deploy*
*Deploy* is a *Passive Ability* and a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
*Deploy* is present on Gear.

*Deploy* is short for “This may be played or created to any battlefield,” “Play or create this only to a battlefield,” “If this is not a unit, it is not recalled in cleanups,” and “When an opponent holds here, kill this.”
*Deploy* grants permission for *Gear* to be played to any *Battlefield,* including enemy occupied and open battlefields.
*Gear* with *Deploy* can be *Moved* by appropriate effects.

*Non-Unit Gear* with *Deploy* are not recalled from *Battlefields* in step 5 of a *Cleanup.*
  *See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.*
Multiple instances of *Deploy* are redundant.
*Deploy,* and whether or not a card has *Deploy,* is a characteristic of the card and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
*Disarm*
*Disarm* is a *Triggered Ability* keyword.
*Disarm* is present on *Units.*
*Disarm* is an *Attack Trigger.*
*Disarm* is formatted as “Disarm X.”
The X is referenced in the functional text of the ability.
The X is referred to as the *Disarm Value.*
If X is omitted, it is presumed to be 1.
*Disarm* is functionally short for “When I attack, give an enemy unit here -X [M] this turn.”
Regardless of how many instances of the *Disarm* keyword a unit has, it will only trigger once using the total *Disarm Value.*

If a *Unit* has *Disarm,* or has been granted *Disarm,* and is granted *Disarm* by an additional source, the *Disarm Value* of all granted *Disarm* keywords is summed.
  Example: Clanging Sentry reads “Your Mechs have [Disarm].” If you play a second Clanging Sentry, both of them will have Disarm 2.
*Disarm,* and whether or not a unit has *Disarm,* is a characteristic of the Unit and may be checked or referenced by other Game Effects.
*Show Off*
*Show Off* is a *Passive Ability* keyword.
*Show Off* is normally present on *Cards.*
*Show Off* is formatted as “[Show Off] [Object].”

The “[Object]” in this ability could be one object or multiple; object/s of a given type; or it could have further specifications on qualities of the object/s. The object in question could be *Game Objects* on the board or cards in hand.
  *Examples:*
  A card reads “[Show Off] a unit.”
  A card reads “[Show Off] a card with Energy cost [7] or more.”
  A card reads “[Show Off] five units with different names.”
*Show Off* is functionally short for “As you play [me/this], you may reveal [Object] from your hand and/or pick [Object] from among friendly game objects on the board.”

*Showing Off* one or more *Cards* or *Game Objects* in this way can be referenced by linked abilities and instructions.
  *Example:* A unit reads in part “[Show Off] five units with different names,” and “When you play me, kill all other units. If you showed off, the next unit you play this turn costs [1] less for each killed unit.”

The decision of whether or not to *Show Off* is made by the controller of the chain item with *Show Off* during the process of finalizing it.
  *See rule 355. Make Relevant Choices for more information.*

If [Object] is a set of *Cards* or *Game Objects,* that set can be composed of *Game Objects* on the board as well as *Cards* in hand, as long as the composed set satisfies the *Show Off* condition.
  *Example:* A unit reads in part “[Show Off] five units with different names.” When showing off as part of playing that unit, units may be revealed from hand or picked from among friendly units on the board, as long as the group of units picked and revealed satisfies the specified quality.

If some or all of the [Object] set leave the appropriate zones during the finalization process after being shown off, it will not prevent the source of the *Show Off* ability from becoming a *Finalized Chain Item.*
  *Example:* A spell reads “[Show Off] a Mech” and “As an additional cost to play this, discard 1.” When finalizing the spell, the same Mech being shown off can be discarded to the mandatory additional cost without preventing the spell from being finalized.

Linked abilities and instructions can reference information about the shown off object/s.
  *Example:* Primordial Roar is a spell that reads “[Show Off] a unit,” and “If you showed off a unit, deal damage equal to that unit's Might to a unit.”

The information referenced in this way is checked when the card/s in question are shown off during finalization. Any later changes to the shown off objects will not be considered.
  *Example:* Primordial Roar is played showing off a friendly unit with 4 [M] and an enemy unit with 3 [M]. In reaction to Primordial Roar, an opponent plays Frigid Touch, giving the friendly unit -2 [M] this turn. Because the information was checked when the friendly unit was shown off, the spell still deals 4 damage to the enemy unit, killing it.
Multiple instances of *Show Off* are treated separately.

If a linked effect or instruction refers to an instance of *Show Off,* it refers to the keyword granted by the same source unless specified otherwise or there is no keyword granted by the same source. If the linked effect or instruction specifies information about the shown off card, it is linked to only that instance of the *Show Off* keyword. If there is no linked keyword, an ability that references showing off is linked to all *Show Off* keywords on the appropriate card.
  *Example:* A card reads in part “Spells you play have ‘[Show Off] a Mighty unit.’ and ‘If you showed off, this costs [A] less.” If a spell that reads in part “[Show Off] a spell with Energy cost [7] or more,” and “If you showed off, this can’t be countered.” is played by the same controller, showing off a Mighty unit will not be sufficient to satisfy both abilities that reference showing off because they refer to instances of the show off keyword granted by different sources.
*Show Off,* and whether or not a card has *Show Off,* is a characteristic of the card and may be checked or referenced by other *Game Effects.*
